questions.prompt: An EICR finds a 32 A circuit feeding an electric shower. Measured Zs = 0.45 Ω; table 41.3 max for the device = 1.37 Ω; 80% = 1.10 Ω. The result:

options.A: Satisfactory — comfortable margin against the rule of thumb
options.B: Unsatisfactory — borderline

questions.explanation: 0.45 Ω is well below 1.10 Ω. The shower circuit has good fault disconnection capability; bonding (typically supplementary equipotential in the bathroom or 30 mA RCD covering the circuit) provides the additional protective layer.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation that 'the consumer unit's main earthing terminal is on a fully terminated 16 mm² conductor to the gas pipe' is typically:

options.A: Satisfactory — 16 mm² main bonding is generously sized; the termination at the gas pipe is correct (typically a BS 951 clamp on the consumer side of the meter)
options.B: Unsatisfactory — over-sized
options.C: Unsatisfactory — should be on the meter

questions.explanation: 16 mm² main bonding on TN-C-S is acceptable and sometimes specified by DNOs for high-fault supplies. Termination at the consumer side of the gas meter using a BS 951 clamp is standard. The arrangement is satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Periodic inspection of an EV charger circuit finds a Type B RCD upstream of a 7 kW unit. Typical observation:

options.A: Satisfactory — Type B RCD detects AC, pulsating DC and smooth DC residual current; suitable for EV charger DC fault scenarios
options.B: Unsatisfactory — Type B not allowed

questions.explanation: Type B RCDs detect across the full residual-current waveform spectrum — AC, pulsating DC, and smooth DC. EV charger circuits commonly require Type B (or Type A with built-in 6 mA DC detection on the unit). The arrangement is satisfactory.

questions.prompt: An EICR records 'IR test results: L-N >999 MΩ, L-E >999 MΩ, N-E 0.5 MΩ'. The defensible interpretation:

options.A: Investigate the N-E fault — there is insulation breakdown specifically between the neutral and earth somewhere in the circuit
options.B: Pass — average above 1 MΩ

questions.explanation: N-E low IR with high L-N and L-E means the fault is specifically between the neutral conductor and earth. Common causes: connected appliance with N-E leakage, damaged insulation in the neutral run, or a wiring fault. Disconnect loads, retest, then locate.

questions.prompt: On a TN-C-S installation, broken-PEN risk requires:

options.A: Adequate main protective bonding (sized per Reg 544.1) so that during a broken-PEN event the entire installation rises with the bonded services, eliminating dangerous touch voltages
options.B: Just an RCD

questions.explanation: Broken-PEN risk is the reason main bonding is sized per the supply earth on TN-C-S. The bonding equalises potential between the installation and external services during a broken-PEN event, eliminating the dangerous voltage between two metal items in contact with a person.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds an installation where the loop tester reads Zs at the origin of 0.18 Ω. The supply is TN-C-S. The defensible interpretation:

options.A: Ze ≈ 0.18 Ω is well within the typical TN-C-S 0.35 Ω quoted limit; satisfactory
options.B: Unsatisfactory — too low

questions.explanation: Ze of 0.18 Ω at the origin is comfortably within the typical TN-C-S maximum of 0.35 Ω quoted by DNOs. Distance from the substation, conductor sizing in the supply, and any parallel earth paths all influence the actual value.

questions.prompt: On a 6 A Type B MCB, the table Zs maximum (BS 7671 Table 41.3) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Type B 6 A: Im = 5 × 6 = 30 A. Zs = 230/30 = 7.67 Ω at full operating temperature. 80% rule of thumb gives 6.13 Ω measured cold. Lighting circuits typically have plenty of margin against this figure.

questions.prompt: An EICR identifies a fixed appliance fed via a 13 A FCU on a ring final circuit. Typical observation:

options.A: Satisfactory — FCU is the standard means of providing local fault and overload protection for fixed appliances on a 32 A ring; circuit complies with Appendix 15
options.B: Unsatisfactory — fixed appliances cannot be on a ring
options.C: Unsatisfactory — must be on a dedicated radial

questions.explanation: FCU on a ring is standard practice — Appendix 15 expressly permits fixed appliances on a 32 A ring final via a 13 A FCU. The FCU provides local protection at the appliance's rated current. Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds an installation where supplementary bonding in a kitchen has been installed using 4 mm² conductor. Typical observation:

options.A: Satisfactory — supplementary bonding is typically sized 2.5 mm² (with mechanical protection) or 4 mm² (without), per Reg 544.2
options.B: Unsatisfactory — should be 6 mm²

questions.explanation: Supplementary bonding sizing per Reg 544.2: 2.5 mm² with mechanical protection, 4 mm² without. The 4 mm² conductor is at the upper end of the standard sizing and is satisfactory regardless of mechanical protection arrangement.

questions.prompt: An EICR records 'the inspector measured Zs at three points on a 32 A ring: at the consumer unit, at the midpoint, and at the furthest point. All readings agree within 5%'. Defensible interpretation:

options.A: Satisfactory — readings consistent with a healthy ring; the parallel paths give similar Zs at every point on the ring (this is the protective benefit of the ring topology)
options.B: Suspicious — should vary with distance

questions.explanation: Ring final circuits give similar Zs at every point because of the parallel paths. A radial would show Zs increasing with distance; a ring shows uniform Zs. Consistent readings confirm the ring is intact and the parallel paths are working.

questions.prompt: An EICR identifies a TT installation where the earth electrode is bonded to the consumer unit's earth bar via a 10 mm² conductor with mechanical protection. Typical observation:

options.A: Satisfactory — 10 mm² with mechanical protection meets Reg 543/544 for TT earthing conductors; well-protected against accidental damage
options.B: Unsatisfactory — should be 16 mm²

questions.explanation: Earthing conductor on TT: 16 mm² without mechanical protection; can be reduced when protected. 10 mm² with mechanical protection is satisfactory. Sizing depends on cable size relationship to circuit CPCs and the fault current rating.

questions.prompt: The fundamental purpose of the EICR is:

options.A: To provide a defensible, documented condition assessment of the installation against the current edition of BS 7671, with codes and a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory result that informs the duty holder's responsibilities
options.B: To certify new work

questions.explanation: The EICR is a documented condition assessment. It informs the duty holder of the current state of the installation, codes the observations, and gives a defensible Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory result. EAWR and ESS PRS regulate the wider regime; the EICR is the technical evidence within it.

questions.prompt: A domestic installation has no surge protective device. The client works from home with ordinary computer equipment, but no special medical, safety or commercial risk assessment is available. What is the best classification?

options.A: C1 because all installations without SPDs are immediately dangerous
options.B: C2 because absence of a current protective measure is always potentially dangerous
options.D: C3 where current requirements/risk assessment indicate SPD provision, otherwise possibly no reportable observation; not normally C2 on this fact pattern

questions.explanation: Absence of an SPD is not normally immediate or potential shock/fire danger by itself. It is generally an improvement recommendation when current requirements or risk assessment indicate it should be provided. Ordinary home office equipment alone does not automatically make it C2.

questions.prompt: An HMO has socket-outlet final circuits in bedrooms. No AFDDs are fitted. The consumer unit tests satisfactorily and shows no thermal damage. What is the best classification under current-style guidance?

options.B: C3, unless actual arcing/thermal damage or another defect is found
options.C: C2 in every HMO regardless of condition
options.D: N/A because AFDDs are never considered during EICRs

questions.explanation: Absence of AFDDs in premises where current rules call for them is generally an improvement recommendation when there is no actual defect. If arcing damage, overheating or damaged terminations are found, code those defects separately, commonly as C2.

questions.prompt: At a single-phase TN-C-S intake you measure: L-N prospective short-circuit current 1.42 kA, L-PE prospective earth fault current 1.18 kA, and Ze 0.18 ohm. What PFC value should be recorded at the origin?

options.D: The average of 1.42 kA and 1.18 kA

questions.explanation: The maximum prospective fault current at the origin is the higher of the measured prospective short-circuit current and prospective earth fault current. Here, record 1.42 kA.

questions.prompt: On a TN-S installation, Ze appears to be 0.09 ohm with main bonding connected. With bonding disconnected under controlled conditions, Ze is 0.47 ohm. Which value is Ze?

options.A: 0.09 ohm, because lower values are always more accurate
options.B: The average of both readings
options.D: Neither value can ever be used

questions.explanation: Ze is the external earth fault loop impedance, measured without parallel paths from main bonding influencing the result. The 0.09 ohm value is likely reduced by bonding and other parallel metallic paths. Bonding must be disconnected only with suitable precautions and must be reconnected and verified before leaving.

questions.prompt: A school is having its electrical installation condition-assessed. The correct certification is:

options.B: Electrical Installation Condition Report (EICR)

questions.explanation: An EICR records the condition of an existing installation. EICs and MEIWCs are issued for new work or alterations; PAT applies to portable appliances rather than the fixed installation.

questions.prompt: Which set of forms forms the complete EICR document set?

options.B: EICR plus Schedule of Inspections plus Schedule of Test Results
options.D: EICR plus design risk assessment only

questions.explanation: BS 7671 Appendix 6 model forms: EICR (the headline report), Schedule of Inspections (visual), Schedule of Test Results (numerical). All three are required; the EICR is incomplete without the schedules.

questions.prompt: A factory production line cannot be shut down during normal hours. The inspector should:

options.B: Skip those circuits silently
options.C: Record an Operational Limitation, agree out-of-hours access or a deferred testing plan, and cross-reference it on the EICR

questions.explanation: Operational limitations are routine on commercial/industrial sites. The inspector documents what could not be tested, why, and any agreed plan to revisit. The duty holder must understand the gap before signing off the EICR.

questions.prompt: On an EICR for a hospital ward, the 'Extent of installation covered' should:

options.B: Reflect exactly what was inspected and tested, with anything excluded recorded as an agreed limitation
options.C: Default to a single sample circuit
options.D: Be left blank because it's a complex site

questions.explanation: Healthcare premises are notoriously full of access/operational constraints. The inspector documents both the extent and the limitations precisely — vague entries here create real liability.

questions.prompt: An MEIWC is appropriate for which of the following jobs?

options.A: Replacing a damaged faceplate on an existing socket without altering the circuit
options.B: Installing a brand-new shower circuit
options.C: Adding a fused spur to an existing ring final to feed a new fan

questions.explanation: An MEIWC covers an addition or alteration that does not introduce a new circuit. Adding a new shower circuit needs an EIC; a periodic inspection needs an EICR; a like-for-like accessory swap may not need a certificate at all under some interpretations.

questions.prompt: The 'Operational Limitations' section on an EICR is used for:

options.B: Items the inspector chose not to look at
options.C: Constraints arising from how the installation operates (e.g. circuits that must remain energised) that prevent full inspection or testing

questions.explanation: Operational limitations are physical/process constraints — for example, life-safety circuits in a hospital that cannot be isolated. They differ from agreed limitations, which are scope decisions made with the client.

questions.prompt: A retail unit is being condition-reported. The recommended interval to the next inspection is:

options.B: Decided by the inspector based on installation condition, environment, occupancy and BPG4/IET GN3 guidance

questions.explanation: BPG4 / IET Guidance Note 3 give default maximum intervals. The inspector must adjust them based on what they actually find — heavy retail use with a high-churn fit-out will normally pull the interval in.

questions.prompt: Where the EICR contains C1, C2 or FI observations, the overall outcome must be recorded as:

options.B: Unsatisfactory

questions.explanation: Any single C1, C2 or FI renders the overall classification Unsatisfactory. C3 alone keeps the report Satisfactory but with improvement recommendations. The Unsatisfactory result is the trigger for landlord / duty-holder action.

questions.prompt: If the inspector and the testing engineer are different people on a large EICR, the report should:

options.B: Carry separate sign-offs for inspection, testing and report responsibility
options.C: Be signed by the office manager

questions.explanation: BS 7671 model EICR allows three roles to be signed off separately: the person carrying out the inspection, the person carrying out the testing, and the person responsible for the report. Each accepts responsibility for their part of the work.

questions.prompt: On the Schedule of Inspections for an existing dwelling, items that don't apply to the installation should be:

options.B: Marked ✗ as faults

questions.explanation: Standard convention is ✓ acceptable, ✗ defective and N/A not applicable. Marking ✓ for items that aren't present is misleading and could undermine the report if challenged.

questions.prompt: A privately rented dwelling has had remedial work after an Unsatisfactory EICR. The landlord must obtain:

options.A: Written confirmation from a qualified person that the remedial work has been carried out
options.B: Verbal assurance only
options.D: Nothing — the original EICR is enough

questions.explanation: Under PRS Regulations 2020, written confirmation from a qualified person that the remedial work has addressed the C1/C2/FI items is required, normally within 28 days, and copies must be supplied to the tenant and (on request) the local authority.

questions.prompt: Sampling on an EICR is permitted, but:

options.A: Must be agreed and explicitly recorded as a limitation
options.B: Is implied automatically when the inspector is busy
options.C: Removes the need for any test results

questions.explanation: If less than 100% of an installation is to be inspected/tested, the sample size and basis must be agreed with the client, recorded as an agreed limitation, and the inspector must use BPG4 sampling escalation rules if defects are found in the sample.

questions.prompt: A duty holder asks the inspector to back-date the EICR by a month to cover an insurance gap. The inspector should:

options.A: Comply if the fee is right
options.B: Refuse — the report must reflect the actual inspection date

questions.explanation: Falsifying the inspection date is fraud and would render the report invalid. The inspector signs the document for the date the work was carried out — no exceptions.

questions.prompt: On an EICR, the field 'Reason for the report' typically records:

options.B: Whether the report is a periodic inspection, change of tenancy, insurance requirement, post-incident check, etc.

questions.explanation: The reason for the report shapes the inspector's approach. A change-of-tenancy EICR may focus on tenant-occupied areas; a post-fire check zooms in on the affected zone with appropriate sampling escalation.

questions.prompt: A small office has a recent satisfactory EICR. A new circuit is then added. The correct paperwork is:

options.A: A new EICR for the whole installation
options.B: An EIC for the new circuit

questions.explanation: A new circuit requires an EIC. The previous EICR remains valid for the existing installation. An MEIWC is only for additions/alterations that do not introduce a new circuit.

questions.prompt: The 'Recommended date for the next inspection' on an EICR is:

options.B: Set by the inspector and may be shorter if condition warrants — but cannot exceed BPG4/GN3 default maxima

questions.explanation: The inspector chooses the next-inspection interval based on findings and BPG4/GN3 guidance. It can always be pulled in (e.g. due to environment or condition) but should not be longer than the default for the premises type.

questions.prompt: An agricultural installation with a high level of mechanical and environmental risk would normally be condition-reported:

options.A: Less often than a domestic property
options.B: More often than a domestic property — typical default of 3 years or shorter

questions.explanation: Agricultural premises carry higher risks (livestock, dust, water, mechanical damage) and are typically inspected at shorter intervals — BPG4/GN3 default is around 3 years, with shorter intervals for high-risk areas.

questions.prompt: On the Schedule of Test Results, the column for 'CPC continuity (R2)' records:

options.B: The end-to-end resistance of the circuit protective conductor
options.C: The total earth fault loop impedance

questions.explanation: R2 is end-to-end CPC continuity. It feeds into the verification of (R1+R2) for fault loop calculations and Zs predictions. Recording it on the schedule is mandatory.

questions.prompt: A landlord must supply the EICR to an existing tenant within:

options.B: 28 days

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020: the existing tenant must receive the EICR within 28 days of the inspection. New tenants must receive it before they move in; on request the local authority must receive it within 7 days.

questions.prompt: Photographs supporting the EICR observations:

options.A: Cannot be included in the report
options.B: Are not required by BS 7671 but are good practice for clarity, especially for C1 and C2 observations
options.C: Replace the need for written observations

questions.explanation: Photos are not mandated but support clear communication. A photo of the broken accessory or the missing bond clarifies the C1/C2 finding for the duty holder and reduces disputes about the inspector's interpretation.

questions.prompt: On a hospital EICR, a circuit feeding life-safety equipment cannot be safely isolated. The correct way to record this is:

options.B: An Operational Limitation, with the affected circuits clearly identified and the reason recorded
options.C: Mark it ✓ on the Schedule of Inspections to keep things tidy

questions.explanation: Operational limitations are common in healthcare. The inspector documents the circuits affected and the reason (life-safety, infection control, patient access). The duty holder must understand the gap before accepting the report.

questions.prompt: Which document is required when adding a new shower circuit to an existing dwelling?

options.B: EICR

questions.explanation: A new circuit requires an EIC, with its accompanying schedules. An MEIWC is for changes to an existing circuit; an EICR is for condition assessment of an existing installation.

questions.prompt: The Schedule of Inspections on an EICR is primarily a:

options.B: Tick-box record of visual / observational checks against BS 7671 model items

questions.explanation: The Schedule of Inspections is the visual / observational checklist (typical of Appendix 6 model forms). It complements the Schedule of Test Results (numerical) and the EICR observations (coded findings).

questions.prompt: On a rented domestic EICR, who is responsible for acting on the Unsatisfactory result?

options.B: The landlord (duty holder)

questions.explanation: Under PRS Regulations 2020, the landlord must arrange remedial work or further investigation within 28 days (or sooner if specified) and supply written confirmation. The inspector reports; the duty holder acts.

questions.prompt: An EICR is being produced after a small fire in one office area. The Reason for the Report should record:

options.B: Post-incident inspection following fire damage in the office area

questions.explanation: The Reason for the Report shapes the scope. A post-incident inspection focuses on the affected area, with sampling escalation rules applied if defects are found, and limitations recorded for areas not inspected.

questions.prompt: An EICR is being prepared for a small B&B let on a short-term basis. The applicable maximum routine interval is:

options.B: 3 years (typical for non-domestic / commercial buildings used by the public)

questions.explanation: Commercial premises (including small B&Bs / hotels) typically default to 5 years, but where there is significant public access or higher risk a 3-year interval is common. The inspector must adjust based on condition and use.

questions.prompt: An EICR's 'Departures from BS 7671' section is used for:

options.A: Reasoned alternatives that achieve at least the same level of safety as the standard
options.B: Excuses for non-compliance

questions.explanation: Departures must be technically justified and signed off by a competent person. They are not a route to lower safety, but to recognise alternative solutions that meet or exceed BS 7671's intent. Departures must be clearly recorded on the EICR.

questions.prompt: A change-of-tenancy EICR is being undertaken on a privately rented dwelling. The landlord has the previous report from 18 months ago. The inspector should:

options.A: Refuse — the dwelling has had an EICR recently
options.B: Treat the new inspection as required because of the change of tenancy and produce a fresh EICR

questions.explanation: Under PRS Regulations 2020, a fresh EICR must be supplied to the new tenant before they move in if the existing one is approaching expiry, but in practice many landlords commission a new EICR on each tenancy change to demonstrate compliance. The new report is the inspector's own work, not a re-issue.

questions.prompt: Operational vs Agreed Limitations on an EICR — the difference is:

options.B: Operational limitations stem from how the installation is run; Agreed limitations are scope decisions made jointly with the client

questions.explanation: Operational = constraints from operation (cannot isolate critical kit). Agreed = inspector and client agree what is in/out of scope (e.g. tenant's bedroom not accessed). Both belong on the EICR; both must be specific.

questions.prompt: An EICR reports an item ✓ on the Schedule of Inspections that the inspector did not actually check. The risk is:

options.B: The inspector takes responsibility for an item they have not verified, and the report is misleading

questions.explanation: Marking ✓ creates a positive declaration that the item is acceptable. If the inspector hasn't checked it, that's fraudulent and dangerous. Use N/A or record an agreed limitation instead.

questions.prompt: A duty holder asks for a 'pass' EICR with no observations because they feel the property is fine. The inspector must:

options.B: Record observations honestly and code them per BPG4 — the report cannot be tailored to a desired outcome
options.C: Issue a Minor Works Certificate instead

questions.explanation: The inspector's signature is a professional declaration. Suppressing observations to please a client exposes the inspector to legal liability if injury later results — and fundamentally undermines the safety system the EICR exists to support.

questions.prompt: On a 3-phase EICR, missing main protective bonding to a metallic gas service is recorded as:

options.A: An observation in the EICR's coded list
options.B: A note on the Schedule of Test Results only
options.D: Not at all if the rest of the system passes

questions.explanation: All defects feed the coded observations list on the EICR. Bonding omissions to extraneous-conductive-parts are typically C2 (potentially dangerous). The Schedule of Test Results captures readings; the EICR observations capture defects.

questions.prompt: A small dwelling EICR with no observations is recorded as:

options.B: Unsatisfactory by default

questions.explanation: An EICR with no C1/C2/C3/FI observations is Satisfactory. The recommended next-inspection date still has to be set, schedules still have to be completed, and the inspector still signs and dates the report.

questions.prompt: A school EICR identifies an Unsatisfactory outcome with three C2 items. The duty holder under HSWA 1974 / EAWR 1989 should:

options.B: Plan and execute remedial work within a reasonable timescale, prioritising by risk and recording action taken

questions.explanation: Schools are non-domestic premises subject to HSWA 1974 and EAWR 1989. The duty holder (typically the head teacher / governor body via their FM team) must act on Unsatisfactory findings within a sensible timeframe and keep records of the remediation.

questions.prompt: An MEIWC is being issued for a fused spur added to a ring final. The MEIWC must include:

options.A: A full inspection of the entire dwelling
options.B: Test results for the part of the existing circuit affected by the addition (Zs, polarity, R1+R2, IR as relevant), and confirmation that the existing circuit's protective measures remain effective
options.C: Just a description of the new accessory
options.D: A schedule of test results for every circuit in the dwelling

questions.explanation: An MEIWC requires testing of the circuit affected by the work, with confirmation that the existing protective measures remain effective. It is not a full periodic inspection — that's the EICR's job.

questions.prompt: A factory floor EICR has a 'Limitations' section recording: 'Cabinets MCC-3 to MCC-6 not opened due to live-working restrictions'. The duty holder should understand that:

options.B: Those cabinets were not inspected/tested and any defects within them are outside the scope of this report
options.C: The next EICR can ignore them too
options.D: The inspector will return free of charge

questions.explanation: Limitations explicitly remove items from the inspector's declared scope. The duty holder must arrange separate access (out-of-hours, planned shutdown) to fill the gap or accept the residual risk.

questions.prompt: An EICR cover sheet shows the inspector's company contact details. The reason is:

options.B: So the duty holder can contact the inspector or the firm regarding queries, remedial work or insurance traceability

questions.explanation: Traceability matters when the report is queried, audited or relied on years later. Insurers and local authorities may need to verify who carried out the work, and the firm's professional indemnity sits behind the signature.

questions.prompt: An EICR identifies one C3 and no C1/C2/FI items. The overall outcome is recorded as:

options.B: Satisfactory — with improvement recommendations

questions.explanation: C3 alone does not make the report Unsatisfactory. The outcome is Satisfactory and the C3 is recorded as an improvement recommendation. Only C1, C2 or FI drive an Unsatisfactory result.

questions.prompt: On an EICR for a privately rented dwelling, the landlord must supply a copy of the report to the local authority on request within:

options.B: 7 days

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020: existing tenant within 28 days; new tenant before move-in; local authority within 7 days of a written request. The landlord must keep records to demonstrate compliance.

questions.prompt: A 'sample' EICR (only a percentage of circuits inspected and tested) is acceptable provided that:

options.B: The sample is agreed in writing, the basis is recorded, and BPG4 sampling escalation is applied if defects are found
options.C: The inspector ticks every item ✓ for tidiness
options.D: Sampling is never acceptable on an EICR

questions.explanation: Sampling is allowed but must be transparent: agreed up-front, recorded, and escalated when defects appear in the sample (per BPG4). A silent sample dressed up as a whole-installation report is misleading and creates real liability.

questions.prompt: An office EICR includes the addition of a circuit and a periodic inspection in the same visit. The correct paperwork is:

options.A: Both an EIC for the new circuit and an EICR for the existing installation
options.B: An EICR alone

questions.explanation: New work and condition assessment are different deliverables. The new circuit is documented on an EIC; the existing installation is documented on an EICR. Combining them into a single document is incorrect.

questions.prompt: An MEIWC issued for an alteration to an existing circuit must:

options.B: Confirm that the protective measures of the existing circuit remain effective and include the relevant test results
options.C: Include test results for every circuit in the building

questions.explanation: An MEIWC declares that the alteration is safe and that the parent circuit's protective measures still work. It includes Zs, R1+R2 (where applicable), polarity, IR for the affected length, and a description of the work.

questions.prompt: A factory EICR identifies that one motor circuit cannot be tested live. The most appropriate place to record this is:

options.B: In the Operational Limitations section, with the circuit clearly identified
options.C: In the Schedule of Inspections only

questions.explanation: Operational limitations belong on the EICR itself so they sit alongside the observations and the next-inspection date. The duty holder cannot miss them when reviewing the report.

questions.prompt: Where the report finds nothing wrong, the inspector still must:

options.B: Complete the EICR, the Schedule of Inspections and the Schedule of Test Results, sign, date and set the next-inspection interval

questions.explanation: A clean EICR still has all the deliverables — the absence of observations doesn't shorten the document set. The schedules are evidence that the inspector actually did the work that justifies the Satisfactory result.

questions.prompt: On an EICR for a school, the agreed limitations field reads 'Boiler-room circuits not inspected — locked, key with FM contractor unavailable'. This means:

options.B: The circuits are explicitly outside the scope of the report and the duty holder needs to arrange a follow-up to cover them
options.C: The inspector will return free of charge later
options.D: The EICR is automatically Unsatisfactory because of the limitation

questions.explanation: An agreed limitation excludes from scope. It does not classify the missed circuits as good or bad — they are unknown. The duty holder must follow up if they want full coverage.

questions.prompt: A retail unit EICR is to be carried out outside trading hours. This is best handled by:

options.A: Recording an Operational Limitation if it cannot be arranged
options.B: Agreeing the out-of-hours visit up-front and noting the timing on the EICR

questions.explanation: Many commercial EICRs require out-of-hours work. The inspector and duty holder agree access in advance; the report records the date and the arrangements where they affect the scope.

questions.prompt: An EIC requires the test results to demonstrate that the new installation:

options.A: Has been used for at least 12 months
options.B: Complies with BS 7671 at the time of certification

questions.explanation: An EIC is the design-and-build sign-off for compliance with the current edition of BS 7671 at the certification date. Future EICRs are separate condition checks and may apply later editions of the standard.

questions.prompt: A school EICR notes ten C3 items but no C1, C2 or FI. The overall result is:

options.B: Unsatisfactory because there are too many C3s

questions.explanation: C3 quantity does not change the outcome — the report is Satisfactory regardless of how many C3s appear. A pattern of C3s does, however, signal an investment case the duty holder should consider.

questions.prompt: A privately rented dwelling EICR was issued 4 years and 11 months ago. The landlord should commission:

options.B: A new EICR before the 5-year anniversary, to maintain compliance with PRS Regulations 2020

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020 mandate a routine EICR at least every 5 years. The landlord arranges the new inspection before expiry to avoid a compliance gap and to give time for any remedial work.

questions.prompt: When a landlord receives an Unsatisfactory EICR, the timescale to complete remedial or further investigation work is:

options.B: 28 days from the inspection, or sooner if specified by the report

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020: 28 days from the inspection (or sooner if the report specifies). Written confirmation must be supplied to the tenant within 28 days of completion, and to the local authority on request within 7 days.

questions.prompt: A factory has a series of identical packaging machines fed from individual circuits. For sampling purposes, the inspector should:

options.A: Inspect every machine individually with no sampling allowed
options.B: Agree a sample with the client (e.g. 25%), record it as an agreed limitation, and apply BPG4 escalation if defects are found in the sample

questions.explanation: BPG4 supports sampling on installations with repetitive elements. The inspector and client agree the size, record it on the EICR, and the inspector escalates the sample (or moves to 100%) if defects exceed the threshold.

questions.prompt: An EICR is being prepared for a property that has changed use from residential to small commercial office. The applicable inspection interval defaults to:

options.B: 5 years for offices (typical), with adjustment for actual condition and use

questions.explanation: Offices typically default to 5 years per BPG4/IET GN3, adjusted by inspector judgement. The inspector will also consider whether the change of use exposed the existing wiring to new mechanical or environmental risks.

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, missing main protective bonding to the gas service is normally listed:

options.B: In the EICR observations section, coded C2
options.C: On the Schedule of Inspections only as a tick

questions.explanation: Bonding omissions are coded observations. Missing bonding to an extraneous-conductive-part such as a gas service is typically C2 (potentially dangerous) under BPG4 — it doesn't kill anyone today, but a future fault could make exposed metalwork live.

questions.prompt: An EICR's 'Summary of the condition of the installation' is best written as:

options.B: A short, plain-English overview the duty holder can read and act on

questions.explanation: The summary translates the technical findings into language the duty holder can use. "The installation is generally in fair condition; however, there are two C2 observations that must be remedied within 28 days" is more useful than a regulation list.

questions.prompt: An EIC issued for new work in a dwelling triggers a notification under Building Regulations Part P (England) when:

options.B: Only for notifiable works (e.g. new circuits, special locations) — typically discharged via a registered competent person scheme
options.D: Only when a Minor Works Certificate is also issued

questions.explanation: Part P (England, post-2013) limits notifiable works mainly to new circuits and certain special-location work. Registered competent person schemes self-certify; otherwise Building Control notification applies. EICRs are not Part P notifiable.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation that recommends the consumer unit be upgraded to provide RCD protection on every final circuit (where currently only sockets benefit) would be coded:

options.B: C2
options.C: C3 (improvement recommended in line with current edition)

questions.explanation: BPG4: where the previous installation complied at the time, but the current edition requires more (e.g. RCD on lighting circuits in dwellings), the appropriate code is usually C3. The installation is not dangerous as installed, but improvement is recommended.

questions.prompt: Where the existing wiring is the older red/black colour code, the EICR should:

options.B: Treat it as compliant for its era and code only the actual condition concerns; identification at boundaries between old and new colours must be clear
options.D: Recoded the entire installation before reporting

questions.explanation: Old colours are not in themselves a defect. Where mixed colours appear in the same enclosure, identification at the joint is essential — usually a C2/C3 depending on whether the current identification is dangerous or just untidy.

questions.prompt: On an MEIWC for an additional socket, the absence of an installation-wide IR test is:

options.A: A reason to refuse the certificate
options.B: Acceptable — only the affected circuit needs to be tested for the alteration
options.C: Always required for the whole property

questions.explanation: An MEIWC is scoped to the affected circuit. Whole-installation IR is the EICR's domain. The MEIWC confirms the alteration is safe and the parent circuit's protective measures still work.

questions.prompt: An EICR records 'Operational Limitations: data centre suite circuits not isolated due to client's no-shutdown requirement'. The duty holder should:

options.B: Treat the suite as outside the EICR scope and arrange a planned-maintenance window for inspection at a future date

questions.explanation: The duty holder retains the obligation under HSWA 1974 / EAWR 1989 to maintain safety. Operational limitations push the responsibility back onto them to plan the eventual coverage and act on any inferred risks in the meantime.

questions.prompt: Where the number of C3s is high but no C1/C2/FI exist, the inspector's commentary should:

options.B: Mark the report Satisfactory but draw attention to the pattern of C3s and recommend planned remedial investment

questions.explanation: C3 quantity doesn't shift the outcome, but the inspector should signal the pattern in the summary so the duty holder understands the cumulative case for upgrading. That's the value of professional judgement on top of the codes.

questions.prompt: An EICR cover sheet records the report's 'Date of inspection'. The inspector must:

options.A: Use the date the report was emailed
options.B: Use the date the inspection actually took place
options.C: Use the date the EICR document was created in the office
options.D: Use any date that is convenient for the client

questions.explanation: The inspection date governs many statutory clocks — landlord's 28-day remedial deadline, next-inspection interval and admissibility of the report. It must reflect the day the inspector was on site.

questions.prompt: On a small dwelling EICR, the ratings of the consumer unit's BS EN 60898 MCBs are recorded:

options.B: On the Schedule of Test Results, alongside circuit identification, type and rating

questions.explanation: The Schedule of Test Results includes circuit ID, location, type/rating of protective device, conductor sizes, polarity, R1+R2, IR, Zs, RCD and other relevant entries. It must be specific enough that someone else could re-test and reproduce the readings.

questions.prompt: On a hospital EICR, an Operational Limitation has been recorded for theatre circuits. The duty holder asks whether the report still gives them coverage. The honest answer is:

options.B: No — the limitation explicitly excludes those circuits, and a separate plan is needed to cover them
options.C: Yes — the inspector silently inspected them anyway
options.D: No — the report is automatically Unsatisfactory

questions.explanation: Operational limitations carve out scope. The duty holder retains the legal obligation under HSWA 1974 / EAWR 1989 and must plan a route — out-of-hours, scheduled maintenance window — to fill the gap.

questions.prompt: An EICR is being undertaken on an agricultural building. The default routine interval is typically:

options.B: 3 years (BPG4/GN3 default for agricultural environments)

questions.explanation: Agricultural premises sit at the more onerous end of the inspection-interval range due to environmental and mechanical risk. Three years is the typical default; the inspector pulls it shorter where condition or use justifies.

questions.prompt: A privately rented dwelling has had no EICR since the property was let in 2018. The landlord's compliance position under PRS Regulations 2020 is:

options.A: Compliant — only required from new tenancies
options.B: Non-compliant — regulations applied to existing tenancies from April 2021 and require an EICR at least every 5 years
options.D: Compliant only because the tenant has been there a long time

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020 applied to new tenancies from 1 July 2020 and to existing tenancies from 1 April 2021. A landlord without an EICR since 2018 is overdue and must rectify the position immediately.

questions.prompt: On the Schedule of Inspections, an item that is non-compliant should be:

options.B: ✗ and cross-referenced to a coded observation on the EICR

questions.explanation: ✗ marks a defective item; it must be tied back to a coded observation on the EICR (C1/C2/C3/FI) so the reader can trace from the schedule to the description and the action required.

questions.prompt: The inspector needs to record that the upstream supply was a TN-S earthing system. Where does this go?

options.A: Nowhere — the inspector ignores supply characteristics
options.B: On the EICR cover under 'Supply characteristics and earthing arrangements'
options.C: On the Schedule of Test Results only

questions.explanation: Supply characteristics (system type, voltage, frequency, fault level, Ze, prospective fault current) are recorded on the EICR cover. They drive design verification (Zs limits, fault loop, RCD necessity) for the rest of the report.

questions.prompt: An EICR with one C2 and several C3s is overall:

options.B: Unsatisfactory because of the C2

questions.explanation: A single C2 (or C1 or FI) renders the report Unsatisfactory regardless of the C3 count. Once the C2 is remedied and confirmed, the duty holder can update the position with the qualified person's written confirmation.

questions.prompt: On an EICR for a domestic property, an extension lead trailing through the kitchen is:

options.B: Not part of the fixed installation — the inspector may comment in the summary but it is outside the EICR scope

questions.explanation: Portable / non-fixed equipment is outside the EICR scope. The inspector may flag a hazard like a daisy-chain lead in the summary or recommend a PAT-style separate review, but it doesn't drive a coded observation on the fixed installation.

questions.prompt: An office block EICR records 'Agreed limitation: tenant suite 4F not accessed; tenant could not be reached'. The duty holder must:

options.B: Treat the suite as outside scope and arrange access for a follow-up inspection

questions.explanation: An agreed limitation excludes from scope. The duty holder is on the hook to arrange the missed access — the inspector cannot inspect what they can't reach, and a written limitation is what protects both parties.

questions.prompt: On the Schedule of Test Results, the column for 'Maximum permitted Zs' is:

options.B: The maximum Zs allowed by BS 7671 for the protective device and disconnection time

questions.explanation: Maximum permitted Zs is taken from BS 7671 Table 41.3 (or equivalent), corrected for temperature and supply tolerance as appropriate. Comparing measured Zs against permitted Zs is the headline check for ADS adequacy.

questions.prompt: An MEIWC includes a 'Description of work' field. It should be:

options.B: Specific (e.g. 'fused spur added to ring final circuit RFC-2 in kitchen, feeding new wall-mounted boiler')

questions.explanation: A specific description ties the certificate to the work and enables future inspection / fault finding. Vague descriptions are useless and undermine the certificate's audit value.

questions.prompt: A landlord receives an Unsatisfactory EICR with one C1. The first thing they should do is:

options.B: Confirm with the inspector what was made safe on the day, then arrange permanent remedial work and obtain written confirmation as soon as possible

questions.explanation: On a C1 the inspector should already have made safe (typically by isolation) and notified the duty holder same day. The landlord arranges permanent fix, gets written confirmation from a qualified person, and supplies it to the tenant.

questions.prompt: A retail unit EICR includes circuits that have been added since the previous report without certification. Those circuits should be:

options.B: Inspected and tested as part of the EICR, with their lack of original certification noted as a coded observation (typically C3)

questions.explanation: Uncertified additions still belong to the existing installation and fall within EICR scope. The lack of original certification can be a C3 documentation finding; any actual technical defects feed their own observations with appropriate codes.

questions.prompt: An EICR 'Reason for the report' field reads 'Sale of property'. The inspector should:

options.A: Inspect only the rooms the buyer cares about
options.B: Carry out a full EICR with all standard schedules; sale-of-property does not change scope unless agreed and recorded

questions.explanation: Sale-of-property is just a reason for instructing the EICR; it doesn't shrink the scope. If sampling or limitations are wanted, they must be agreed and recorded explicitly.

questions.prompt: On the Schedule of Test Results, the column for RCD test records:

options.B: Tripping times at 1×IΔn and 5×IΔn (and the no-trip at IΔn/2 confirmation as appropriate)
options.C: Just whether it tripped at all

questions.explanation: The schedule captures actual tripping times against the BS 7671 limits — typically ≤300 ms at 1×IΔn for general use and ≤40 ms at 5×IΔn for additional protection. The schedule must show numeric values where measured.

questions.prompt: The 'Recommended interval until next inspection' on an EICR can be longer than 5 years for which premises type?

options.B: Industrial premises with low risk and good condition (some BPG4 categories allow up to 10 years)

questions.explanation: BPG4/GN3 give longer default intervals (up to ~10 years) for some industrial or owner-occupied premises in good condition. PRS rented domestic is capped at 5 years; high-risk premises pull intervals shorter.

questions.prompt: An MEIWC issued for a kitchen-circuit alteration must include test results for:

options.B: The altered circuit only — Zs, R1+R2, IR, polarity and operation of any related RCD as relevant

questions.explanation: MEIWC testing is scoped to the affected circuit. Whole-property testing is the EICR's job. The MEIWC certifies that the alteration is safe and that the parent circuit's protective measures still work.

questions.prompt: On an EICR for a privately rented dwelling, the landlord must supply the new tenant with a copy of the latest EICR:

options.B: Before the new tenant occupies the property

questions.explanation: PRS Regulations 2020: new tenants must receive the EICR before occupation; existing tenants within 28 days; local authority within 7 days of written request. Landlords typically include the EICR in the new-tenancy pack alongside the gas safety certificate.

questions.prompt: An EICR is being produced for a holiday let. The applicable Regulations primarily are:

options.A: PRS Regulations 2020 (England) for short-term lets (varies — many short-term lets fall outside PRS Regs scope; HSWA 1974 / EAWR 1989 generally apply)
options.B: Building Regulations Part P only

questions.explanation: Short-term lets sit in a complex regulatory space — PRS Regulations 2020 cover assured / shorthold tenancies and licences but many holiday lets fall outside the strict definition. HSWA 1974 / EAWR 1989 apply to non-domestic / commercial use. The inspector should note the regime that applies and write the report to suit.

questions.prompt: A ring final circuit gives end-to-end readings r1 = 0.46 ohm, rn = 0.47 ohm and r2 = 0.78 ohm. The highest measured R1+R2 using the figure-of-eight method is 0.31 ohm. Is this plausible?

options.A: No, because R1+R2 must equal r1 + r2
options.B: No, because R1+R2 must equal r2 only
options.C: No, because the neutral reading must be used instead of r2
options.D: Yes. Expected R1+R2 is approximately (0.46 + 0.78) / 4 = 0.31 ohm

questions.explanation: For the ring final figure-of-eight test, the expected socket R1+R2 value is approximately (r1 + r2) / 4. Here that is 1.24 / 4 = 0.31 ohm, so the result is plausible.

questions.prompt: A 32 A ring final has r1 = 0.42 ohm, rn = 0.42 ohm and r2 = 0.69 ohm. Most sockets give R1+R2 around 0.28 ohm, but one double socket gives 0.81 ohm. Polarity is correct and Zs is just within the maximum. What is the best response?

options.A: Ignore it because Zs is within the maximum
options.B: Investigate; possible long spur, spur from spur, loose/high-resistance CPC connection, damaged conductor or socket not on the ring
options.D: Record N/A because spurs are not inspected

questions.explanation: Expected ring values are about (0.42 + 0.69) / 4 = 0.28 ohm. One socket at 0.81 ohm is abnormal. Zs being just acceptable does not remove the need to investigate the actual circuit arrangement and CPC condition. Classification depends on what is found: no code for a compliant spur, C2 for a loose/damaged/unsafe arrangement, or FI if it cannot be determined.

questions.prompt: A domestic lighting circuit with smart dimmers, LED drivers and electronic switches gives L-N insulation resistance at 500 V of 0.72 M ohm, L+N to E at 500 V of >299 M ohm, and L-N at 250 V with equipment connected of 1.4 M ohm. What is the best report treatment?

options.A: Automatically C2 because one value is below 1 M ohm
options.B: Automatically C1 because electronic loads are connected
options.C: Record the limitation/test method and results; do not code automatically if the low L-N result is due to connected equipment rather than wiring insulation failure
options.D: Record no insulation resistance values at all

questions.explanation: Connected electronics can depress L-N insulation readings and may be damaged by inappropriate test voltages. The strong L+N to E reading suggests no live-to-earth wiring insulation defect. Record the actual voltage, method and limitation. If fixed wiring still failed with equipment disconnected, that would be a different matter.

questions.prompt: A whole-installation insulation resistance test gives 0.95 M ohm live conductors to earth. Individual circuits are all above 200 M ohm except one at 1.1 M ohm. The premises is a damp agricultural building. What is the best conclusion?

options.A: Not automatically satisfactory; the low global value and one marginal circuit need judgement and possibly further investigation
options.B: Automatically satisfactory because every individual circuit is above 1 M ohm
options.C: Automatically C1 because the global value is below 1 M ohm
options.D: N/A because insulation resistance is not tested in agricultural buildings

questions.explanation: Individual readings matter, but context also matters. A damp agricultural environment and a circuit only just above 1 M ohm may indicate contamination, moisture, damaged accessories or developing insulation failure. Further investigation or an improvement recommendation may be appropriate depending on stability and risk.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Live conductors exposed at junction box in loft, basic insulation damaged'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — danger present, accessible live parts

questions.explanation: Damaged basic insulation with accessible live parts is the textbook C1. The inspector should isolate the affected circuit and label it before leaving site, regardless of whether the loft is normally accessed.

questions.prompt: A bathroom is missing supplementary equipotential bonding and the four conditions of Reg 701.415.2 cannot all be confirmed. The correct code is:

options.B: C2 — protective measure not satisfied, potentially dangerous

questions.explanation: Where 701.415.2 conditions (RCD protection, ADS Zs limits, all CPCs continuous, all extraneous parts bonded back to MET) cannot be confirmed, supplementary bonding is required. Its absence is C2 because a future fault could put extraneous-parts at line potential.

questions.prompt: A 30 mA RCD providing additional protection trips correctly at 5×IΔn but takes 350 ms at 1×IΔn (BS 7671 limit ≤300 ms). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — protective measure impaired

questions.explanation: 350 ms at 1×IΔn is non-compliant — fault-protection performance is degraded. The fact that it tripped at 5×IΔn shows mechanical operation but doesn't fix the issue. C2: replace the device promptly.

questions.prompt: An accessory has a chipped corner on the front, with no live parts visible and no risk of progression. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2
options.C: C3 — improvement recommended (cosmetic damage with no danger)

questions.explanation: Cosmetic damage without exposed live parts and without a clear progression risk is C3. The accessory should be replaced when convenient, but the EICR remains Satisfactory if this is the only issue.

questions.prompt: A circuit's IR test reads 0.4 MΩ between line and earth (BS 7671 minimum 1 MΩ for an in-service installation). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (typical) or FI if the cause is genuinely uncertain after isolation of suspect loads

questions.explanation: An IR reading below the BS 7671 minimum is a potentially dangerous condition. The inspector should isolate suspect loads (electronic equipment, RCD electronics) and re-test; if the reading remains low, code C2 and remediate. If the cause cannot be established, FI.

questions.prompt: A label on a consumer unit reads '15A' on a circuit breaker that is actually rated 32A (mismatched label). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (likely) — incorrect labelling could mislead future maintenance and cause the wrong fuse to be substituted

questions.explanation: Misleading identification can cause an incorrect device to be fitted in future maintenance, resulting in an under-rated cable being protected by an over-rated device. BPG4 typically calls this C2 due to the foreseeable hazard.

questions.prompt: Bonding clamp on the gas service is loose and oxidised but still continuous. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — mechanical and electrical reliability of the bond is reduced

questions.explanation: A loose, oxidised clamp could become open under vibration or a future fault. The bonding's protective function is compromised. C2: clean / replace the clamp and re-test.

questions.prompt: On an EICR, an item that was compliant when installed but does not meet a later edition (e.g. lighting circuit without RCD in a new dwelling) is most commonly coded:

options.B: C2
options.C: C3 — improvement recommended (current edition exceeds the original requirement)

questions.explanation: BS 7671 is not retrospective. Where an existing installation complied at the time but later editions have added requirements (e.g. RCD on lighting), the typical EICR call is C3 — improvement recommended, not Unsatisfactory.

questions.prompt: A circuit has no main earth bonding to the structural steel of the building (steel is extraneous-conductive-part, confirmed). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — bonding requirement not met

questions.explanation: Where structural steel is confirmed extraneous-conductive-part it must be bonded to the MET. Its omission is potentially dangerous — a future fault could make the steelwork live. C2 and remedy.

questions.prompt: An MCB has been replaced with one of the wrong type (Type B replaced with Type D for a lighting circuit, with a high Zs that the new device cannot satisfy). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (likely) — disconnection time may not be achieved

questions.explanation: Type D requires lower Zs to achieve magnetic disconnection. If Zs is now above the Type D limit, ADS may not operate within the required time — potentially dangerous. C2: replace with the correct device.

questions.prompt: A circuit has had an additional load connected (e.g. an extra socket on a 32 A ring final) and the cable from the new connection back into the circuit is found to be 1.0 mm² T+E. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — undersized conductor, fault current capacity inadequate

questions.explanation: 1.0 mm² T+E is not suitable for a 32 A ring final spur. The conductor cannot carry the full circuit fault current safely; a fault could cause overheating or fire before the protective device clears. C2: replace with appropriately sized cable.

questions.prompt: A consumer unit is fitted in a normal domestic environment with split-load RCD protection. One RCD does not respond to the inspector's test button. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — but consider C1 if it is the only protective measure
options.D: Satisfactory if mechanical operation can be confirmed

questions.explanation: Failure of an RCD's test mechanism plus failure under instrument testing usually warrants C2; if the RCD provides the only fault protection / additional protection on accessible circuits and is non-functional, the call lifts to C1.

questions.prompt: An old rewireable fuse board is intact and operating, but with no RCD protection on accessible socket-outlets. The most appropriate code (current BS 7671 expects RCD additional protection on socket-outlets used by ordinary persons up to 32 A) is:

options.B: C2 (typical) — additional protection requirement not met for sockets accessible to ordinary persons
options.C: C3 (only if all other protective measures are intact and the installation predates the requirement)
options.D: Satisfactory because the fuse board still works

questions.explanation: BPG4 typically calls absence of RCD additional protection on accessible socket-outlets as C2 in modern dwellings — the protective measure required by current safety expectations is missing. Some inspectors apply C3 if the installation is genuinely unaltered from a much earlier era; current consensus is more often C2.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a circuit's polarity reversed at one socket. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (likely) — a single-pole switch will now break neutral; potentially dangerous in fault scenarios

questions.explanation: Reversed polarity means single-pole protection / switching is in the wrong conductor. Equipment internals can be left at line potential when the switch is off. Typical call is C2; some inspectors lift to C1 if there is foreseeable shock risk.

questions.prompt: A circuit is protected by a 32 A MCB; the cable is 4.0 mm² T+E run in insulation. The maximum continuous current the cable can carry under method 100 (insulated wall) at 70 °C is approximately 27 A. The appropriate EICR code is:

options.B: C2 — overload protection not coordinated, cable could be overloaded under design current

questions.explanation: Cable Iz < In(device) means the protective device cannot guarantee to clear an overload before the cable overheats. Potentially dangerous. C2: redesign the protection or reduce the load.

questions.prompt: A pendant lighting fitting has a wholly missing earth conductor (Class I luminaire with no CPC connected). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — protective measure (fault protection) not satisfied
options.C: C1 if a foreseeable fault could put the metal body at line potential where ordinary persons can touch it
options.D: Either B or C depending on accessibility and the rest of the protective measures

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement here: a Class I fitting with no CPC has no fault protection. If the metalwork is reachable by ordinary persons and could become live under fault, the call is often C1. Where the body is well above reach and other layers (RCD) work, C2 may be appropriate.

questions.prompt: A circuit has been visibly altered (a spur added) but the original certification does not show the alteration. The most appropriate code is:

options.A: C3 (typical) — improvement recommended, lack of recent certification of the alteration
options.B: C1 unless tested

questions.explanation: Lack of certification of an alteration is typically C3 (documentation finding). The actual technical condition of the alteration is then judged on its merits — a spur in undersized cable would attract its own C2.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Cable hung over a sharp metal edge in cupboard, sheath chafed but basic insulation intact'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — mechanical protection compromised, foreseeable progression to exposed live parts

questions.explanation: Chafed sheath with intact basic insulation is the classic 'potentially dangerous' progression. C2 — sleeve/reroute the cable; if the basic insulation is also breached then C1.

questions.prompt: A 30 mA RCD trips at 1×IΔn within 200 ms, and at 5×IΔn within 35 ms. The appropriate EICR record is:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — both readings within BS 7671 limits

questions.explanation: ≤300 ms at 1×IΔn and ≤40 ms at 5×IΔn: both readings within limits. The RCD is operating correctly and the schedule entry is Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: An accessory front plate has its earth tail cut off inside the box. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — fault protection on the accessory is impaired
options.C: C1 if the metal accessory is exposed and a future fault could energise it
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether the metal can become live and is reachable

questions.explanation: BPG4 recognises judgement: a metal faceplate that could become live with no CPC connected is often C1 if reachable. A plastic accessory in a non-conductive setting may be C2. Detail and accessibility drive the call.

questions.prompt: A factory EICR finds a damaged armoured cable gland with the steel wire armour exposed and the inner cores still in place. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (typical) — mechanical protection and earthing reliability of the SWA are compromised
options.C: C1 if the cores are also damaged exposing live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on the condition of the inner cores

questions.explanation: BPG4 demands judgement: a damaged gland on intact cores is C2; if basic insulation is also breached and live parts exposed it is C1. The inspector documents what they see.

questions.prompt: A retail shop has a row of socket-outlets with no RCD additional protection. The shop is open to the public and used by ordinary persons. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — current edition requires RCD additional protection on socket-outlets used by ordinary persons up to 32 A

questions.explanation: BPG4 typically classes the absence of RCD additional protection on accessible socket-outlets in commercial premises used by ordinary persons as C2. The protective measure required for shock protection is missing.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Schedule of Test Results not available from previous works; previous EIC missing'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Missing previous certification is a documentation issue, not a current safety hazard. C3 is the typical call. The inspector will still produce a complete EICR and any technical defects will attract their own codes.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a plastic CU on a wooden backboard in a domestic setting, with terminations that are visibly clean and tight. Under current BPG4 the typical code is:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Current BPG4 puts plastic CUs on wooden backboards (non-DSEAR domestic) at C3 — improvement recommended. The 2017 amendment for metal CUs is not retrospective; the inspector documents the existing state with an improvement recommendation.

questions.prompt: A circuit's measured Zs is 20% above the BS 7671 Table 41.3 limit for the protective device. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — ADS may not operate within the required disconnection time

questions.explanation: Above-limit Zs means the protective device may not disconnect within the required time. The protective measure (ADS) is impaired. C2 — investigate and remedy (clean terminations, replace cable, change device, add RCD).

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, the immersion heater's circuit shows discolouration at the junction box terminations and an FBI burning smell. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — danger present (fire risk from overheating termination)

questions.explanation: Active overheating with a burning smell is a present danger. The inspector should isolate the circuit and label it before leaving site, then code C1 with a clear description.

questions.prompt: An office EICR finds an exposed metal back box in a kitchenette with a cracked plastic faceplate held in place by a single screw, the second screw missing. Live parts are not currently exposed but the faceplate is loose. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — foreseeable progression to exposed live parts

questions.explanation: A loose faceplate with one screw missing will progress quickly to exposed live parts in normal use. Potentially dangerous: C2 — refit the faceplate properly. If the faceplate is already detached so live terminals are reachable, C1.

questions.prompt: An EICR identifies a cable buried in plaster <50 mm from the surface, not in a safe zone, with no RCD additional protection. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — additional protection not provided where required for cables outside safe zones
options.D: Satisfactory if no nail damage is visible

questions.explanation: BS 7671 requires either RCD additional protection or earthed mechanical protection for cables <50 mm deep outside safe zones. Absence of both is C2; the inspector advises adding 30 mA RCD protection or rerouting the cable.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds two MCBs cross-connected at the consumer unit (live conductors swapped between two adjacent circuits) but circuit identification labels still match the original layout. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — incorrect identification could mislead future maintenance

questions.explanation: Mislabelled circuits create a foreseeable hazard during isolation for future work. The protective devices may also no longer match their cable sizes if the swap involved different ratings. C2 — correct the identification or the connection as appropriate.

questions.prompt: A 30 mA RCBO providing both fault protection and additional protection trips at 25 ms at 5×IΔn but does not operate at 1×IΔn within 5 seconds. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (likely) — fault protection performance is impaired
options.D: C1 (where the device is the sole protective measure on accessible circuits)

questions.explanation: Failure at 1×IΔn means the fault-protection function is unreliable. C2 typical, lifting to C1 where the device is the sole protective measure on accessible circuits used by ordinary persons.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a Class II luminaire with a single-pole switch in the line conductor. The most appropriate record is:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended
options.C: Satisfactory — Class II appliances do not require an earth, single-pole line switching is normal

questions.explanation: Class II equipment (double insulation) doesn't need an earth and single-pole line switching is correct UK practice. The inspector confirms basic insulation and double-insulation labelling are intact and records Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: A privately rented dwelling's gas boiler is on its own circuit fed from the consumer unit, with no main protective bonding to the metallic incoming gas service. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — main bonding requirement not met for an extraneous-conductive-part
options.D: Satisfactory if RCD protection is in place

questions.explanation: Missing main bonding to a metallic gas service is potentially dangerous and is the textbook BPG4 C2. Even with RCDs in place, the bonding is the equipotential measure that prevents touch voltages during a fault.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds that a property's main earthing conductor is 10 mm² copper for a 100 A PME supply. BS 7671 Table 54.7 minimum is 16 mm² for PME on a 100 A service. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — earthing conductor under-sized for the supply (PME requires larger CSA)

questions.explanation: Under-sized earthing conductor on a PME supply is potentially dangerous because PME requires the conductor to carry combined earth/neutral fault currents. C2: upgrade to the BS 7671 Table 54.7 minimum (typically 16 mm² for ≤100 A or 25 mm² for higher).

questions.prompt: An EICR records that an accessible socket-outlet has a clear crack across the front face that does not yet expose the live parts but progresses up to within 1 mm of a live terminal. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — foreseeable progression to exposed live parts

questions.explanation: A crack approaching a live terminal will progress to exposure under normal in-service forces (plug insertion / removal). Potentially dangerous: C2. If live parts already accessible, C1.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds the main switch of a domestic consumer unit identified as 'Lighting' instead of the actual function. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Where the misidentification of a main switch could be quickly corrected by anyone present and does not present a current danger, C3 is typical. Where the misidentification is on a critical circuit (e.g. a labelled isolator that does not actually isolate the circuit it claims), the call may rise to C2.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'No earthing arrangement found at the supply intake; no Ze can be measured'. The most appropriate code is:

options.A: C1 — no fault protection means of earthing in place
options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Absence of an earthing arrangement at the supply intake means there is no means of fault protection — a fault could leave exposed-conductive-parts at line potential indefinitely. C1: isolate, notify the duty holder and the DNO, and pursue immediate remedy.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a burnt-out neutral termination at the main distribution board, with the busbar surface discoloured. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (where heat damage is contained, no exposed live parts and the joint can be re-tightened or rebuilt)
options.C: C1 if there is a continuing fire risk or exposed live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on the extent of the damage and the immediate fire risk

questions.explanation: BPG4 again rewards judgement. A localised, cooled discolouration with a sound joint can be C2 (rectify promptly). Active burning, smoke, or exposed live parts shifts the call to C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: A 30 mA RCD providing additional protection on socket-outlets is found to be inoperative (no trip at any test current). The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — additional protection impaired
options.C: C1 — sole protective measure for direct contact has failed; sockets accessible to ordinary persons
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether other protective measures are fully effective

questions.explanation: BPG4: RCD failure is C2 where the RCD is one layer of a complete protective scheme; where the RCD is the sole guarantee against direct contact (e.g. cables in safe zones with no earthed mechanical protection, or sockets used outdoors), the inspector typically lifts to C1.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a circuit's R1+R2 measured at 0.43 Ω and the calculated Zs (Ze + R1+R2) at the limit for the device. Schedule reading is at the limit. The most appropriate record is:

options.B: FI — borderline reading; instrument tolerance / cable temperature could push it over the limit

questions.explanation: Borderline readings invite FI: the inspector may want to re-test under operating temperature, cross-check with the instrument's tolerance, or use the corrected Zs method (0.8×Table 41.3 in some guidance). FI is appropriate while the genuine value is uncertain.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Earthing conductor present at MET but no main protective bonding to incoming water service (metallic, confirmed extraneous-conductive-part)'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — main bonding requirement not met
options.D: Satisfactory because earthing conductor is present

questions.explanation: Bonding and earthing are different things. Main bonding to extraneous-conductive-parts is required to maintain equipotential during a fault. Its absence is potentially dangerous: C2 — install bonding to BS 7671 Table 54.8 sizing.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Twin-and-earth cable run beneath floorboards in dwelling, no mechanical protection, no RCD additional protection'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 (typical) — additional protection requirement not met (per BPG4 / current edition)
options.D: Satisfactory if the cable is a long-standing legacy install

questions.explanation: BS 7671 requires either RCD additional protection or earthed mechanical protection for cables in floors / walls in dwellings used by ordinary persons. Absence of both is C2 per current BPG4. C3 may be applied where the installation is a clearly historic one, but the current consensus is more often C2.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds the consumer unit located in a damp basement with active condensation and signs of corrosion at the busbar. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — environmental conditions degrading the equipment, foreseeable progression to fault
options.C: C1 (if active arcing or exposed live parts)
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement: surface corrosion with no live parts exposed and no arcing is typically C2 (relocate / replace promptly). Active arcing or exposed corrosion damage that exposes live parts is C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: A 30 mA RCD providing additional protection on a socket-outlet circuit measured at 28 ms at 5×IΔn. The most appropriate record is:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: ≤40 ms at 5×IΔn is the BS 7671 limit for additional protection. 28 ms is comfortably within. Schedule entry is Satisfactory; no observation needed.

questions.prompt: On a school EICR, the inspector finds a low-level socket in a corridor with a clear crack and the inner shutter mechanism damaged so the shutters no longer cover the live terminals. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — basic protection compromised, accessible live parts

questions.explanation: Damaged shutters with accessible live terminals fail basic protection, particularly in a school where children may be present. Textbook C1 — isolate the socket and label it before leaving site.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a circuit's IR test reading at exactly 1.0 MΩ between line and earth (BS 7671 minimum). The most appropriate record is:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory but on the limit — investigate before next inspection and consider FI if the cause is unclear

questions.explanation: Exactly at the limit is technically Satisfactory but warrants attention. The inspector may record an FI if the reading is suspiciously borderline and the cause cannot be established (e.g. moisture ingress, electronic loads). Where the reading is stable and explained, Satisfactory with a note suffices.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds that an existing rewireable fuse has been replaced with a length of foil. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — overcurrent protection has effectively been defeated, danger present

questions.explanation: Foil substitution defeats the protective device entirely — a fault could lead to fire before the supply tripped upstream (if at all). The inspector must isolate the circuit, label it and code C1; this is dangerous and the duty holder must be informed immediately.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds an outdoor socket-outlet at a domestic dwelling without RCD additional protection. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — outdoor sockets used by ordinary persons require RCD additional protection (current BS 7671 requirement)
options.D: Satisfactory if the socket has weatherproof shutters

questions.explanation: Outdoor / outside-equipped circuits used by ordinary persons require 30 mA RCD additional protection. A weatherproof enclosure is helpful but doesn't replace RCD. C2 is the typical call.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Spare way in consumer unit — terminal block connected directly to MCB but no cable connected'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — exposed live terminal could be inadvertently energised in a future event (cover removed for maintenance)
options.C: C1 if the live terminal is currently exposed
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether the terminal is now accessible

questions.explanation: BPG4: an unused terminal can be C1 if currently accessible (basic protection failure) or C2 if covered now but a foreseeable maintenance event would expose it. The correct fix is to remove the MCB and blank the way.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a Type B 6 A MCB on a circuit feeding only a small inductive transformer with frequent inrush trips. The most appropriate observation is:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (Type C may be more suitable to avoid nuisance tripping)
options.D: Satisfactory unless the protective requirements of BS 7671 are not met

questions.explanation: If the MCB still provides correct fault and overload protection per BS 7671, the nuisance-tripping issue is a functional / design preference rather than a safety code. The inspector may note a recommendation for a Type C device but this is not strictly an EICR coded observation unless protection is impaired.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation reads 'Hot-water boiler isolator switch fitted but not labelled; switching position uncertain'. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — labelling could mislead emergency isolation

questions.explanation: An unlabelled switch is typically C3 unless its mis-operation could create immediate danger. The inspector recommends labelling per BS 7671 514.1.1, and the report remains Satisfactory unless other observations push it Unsatisfactory.

questions.prompt: An EICR finds a metal cable tray / containment system not connected to the protective earth. The most appropriate code is:

options.B: C2 — extraneous-conductive-part not bonded; foreseeable fault could energise the tray
