options.C: C1 — if live terminals are reachable when probed
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether live terminals are currently accessible

questions.explanation: BPG4: non-functional shutters with live terminals reachable on probe = C1; not currently reachable but unreliable shutters = C2 with prompt remedy.

questions.prompt: TN-C-S supply with PME, no warning notice at consumer unit. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (warning / labelling)

questions.explanation: Missing safety / warning notices are typically C3. Add a PME / TN-C-S warning at the position of the main earthing terminal so future maintenance / DNO operations are correctly informed.

questions.prompt: Cable run beneath floorboards, no mechanical protection, no RCD additional protection. Code (typical):

options.B: C2 — additional protection required by current edition

questions.explanation: BS 7671 requires either RCD additional protection or earthed mechanical protection for cables hidden in floors / walls in dwellings used by ordinary persons. Absence of both is C2.

questions.prompt: Consumer unit located in damp basement with active condensation, surface corrosion. Code:

options.B: C2 — environmental conditions degrading equipment
options.C: C1 if active arcing or exposed corrosion damage exposing live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: BPG4: surface corrosion no exposed live parts no arcing = C2; active arcing / exposed live parts = C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: 30 mA RCD trips in 28 ms at 5×IΔn (limit 40 ms) and is otherwise intact. Record:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Within the 40 ms limit at 5×IΔn = Satisfactory. Schedule entry records the value; no observation needed.

questions.prompt: Cracked socket front face approaching a live terminal (within 1 mm). Code:

options.B: C2 — foreseeable progression to exposed live parts

questions.explanation: A clear crack approaching live terminals will progress to exposure under normal in-service forces. Potentially dangerous (C2). Replace the accessory promptly.

questions.prompt: Junction box in a maintained location with a tape-wrapped connection. Code (typical):

options.B: C2 — joint not made in suitable terminal
options.C: C1 if visibly hot or arcing
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement; cool tape-wrapped joints in proper enclosures are C2; hot / arcing joints lift to C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Bath / basin in a dwelling with plastic plumbing throughout (extraneous-conductive-part status not relevant). No bonding present. Code:

options.B: Satisfactory — plastic plumbing is not extraneous-conductive-part requiring bonding

questions.explanation: Plastic plumbing is not an extraneous-conductive-part. Bonding is therefore not required to it. The EICR confirms the status and records Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Exposed metal back box at a switch position with damaged faceplate; live terminal accessible. Code:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: A live terminal that can be touched presents immediate danger of electric shock. That makes the observation C1, with isolation, warning and prompt notification needed before the installation is left accessible.

questions.prompt: Domestic kitchen with no RCD additional protection on socket-outlets, in active dwelling. Code (typical):

options.A: C3 only if installation is plainly historic
options.B: C2 (typical for an actively used dwelling)
options.D: Either A or B depending on inspector's judgement

questions.explanation: Current consensus is C2 in active dwellings; C3 may be applied to clearly historic untouched installations. The inspector judges based on the installation's age, recent works and use pattern.

questions.prompt: Undersized CPC (1.0 mm² CPC on 4 mm² 32 A radial), no parallel earth path. Code:

options.B: C2 — adiabatic check fails / CPC inadequate for fault current

questions.explanation: Undersized CPC may not survive fault current within device clearance time. C2 — replace with adequately sized CPC or upgrade protective device.

questions.prompt: RCD trips at 5×IΔn but takes >5 s at 1×IΔn. Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection performance impaired
options.C: C1 if sole protective measure on accessible circuits
options.D: Either B or C depending on protective scheme

questions.explanation: Failure at 1×IΔn means fault protection is unreliable. C2 typical, lifting to C1 where the RCD is the sole protective measure on circuits used by ordinary persons.

questions.prompt: TN-S installation with 4 mm² bare main earthing conductor, undersized for current BS 7671 Table 54.7 sizing. Code:

options.B: C2 — earthing conductor inadequate for current fault levels
options.C: C1 if installation has been modified to higher fault levels with the conductor unchanged
options.D: Either B or C depending on supply / fault level

questions.explanation: Undersized main earthing conductor is potentially dangerous; C2 typical. Where the supply has been upgraded to a higher fault level without changing the conductor, the call may rise to C1.

questions.prompt: Dwelling lighting circuit complies with original installation edition but lacks RCD required by current edition. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (current edition exceeds original requirement)

questions.explanation: BS 7671 not retrospective. Where the installation complied at the time but does not match current edition, the typical EICR call is C3 — improvement recommended (e.g. add RCD protection).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an unidentified cable disappearing into a wall, no test access available. Code:

options.B: FI — further investigation required

questions.explanation: FI captures evidence of a possible defect that the inspector cannot diagnose during the inspection. Investigation may use cable detection or open-up access; the EICR is Unsatisfactory until it is done.

questions.prompt: Cosmetic chip on a faceplate, no live parts visible, no risk of progression. Code:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Cosmetic damage with no exposed live parts and no progression risk is C3. The accessory should be replaced when convenient; the EICR remains Satisfactory if this is the only issue.

questions.prompt: Single-pole switch on the line conductor of a Class II luminaire. Record:

options.B: C2
options.D: Satisfactory — Class II equipment doesn't require an earth and single-pole line switching is normal UK practice

questions.explanation: Class II equipment (double insulation) doesn't need an earth. Single-pole line switching is correct UK practice — confirm basic insulation and double-insulation labelling and record Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Cooker socket switched on with no plug, non-functional shutters, live terminals reachable on probe. Code:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Reachable live terminals at an accessible socket = C1. Isolate, label, notify duty holder same day.

questions.prompt: Mains earthing strap broken at the MET (no continuity). Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — fault protection earth path lost

questions.explanation: Open earth at the MET means the entire installation has lost its means of earthing. Fault protection cannot operate. C1 with on-site make-safe / isolation and same-day notification.

questions.prompt: Inspector's IR test reads exactly 1.0 MΩ between line and earth. Record:

options.B: Satisfactory at the limit; investigate cause if borderline trend, consider FI if the reading is suspicious

questions.explanation: Exactly at limit is technically Satisfactory; the inspector may use FI if the reading is borderline and the cause cannot be established. A stable, explained borderline reading is recorded as Satisfactory with a note.

questions.prompt: An MCB (BS EN 60898) Type B 16 A on a circuit feeding only a small inductive transformer with frequent inrush trips. The circuit is intrinsically safe, just nuisance-tripping. EICR record:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (Type C may be more suitable)
options.C: Satisfactory unless protection is impaired; functional issue rather than safety code

questions.explanation: If protection is intact and BS 7671 disconnection times are met, nuisance tripping is a functional preference rather than an EICR-coded defect. The inspector may note a recommendation for a Type C device.

questions.prompt: Hot-water boiler isolator fitted as single-pole switch (BS 7671 typically requires DP isolation). Code:

options.B: C2 — isolation switching incomplete

questions.explanation: DP isolation requirement comes from the need to fully isolate during maintenance. SP isolators leave the neutral connected — potentially dangerous (C2). Replace with DP isolator.

questions.prompt: Crossed circuit IDs at the consumer unit (cables swapped, labels still match original layout). Code:

options.B: C2 — incorrect identification could mislead future maintenance

questions.explanation: Mislabelled circuits create unsafe maintenance switching. The protective devices may also no longer match cable sizes. Potentially dangerous (C2) — correct the identification or rewiring.

questions.prompt: Spare way in CU with MCB still fitted, cable not connected, terminal currently accessible (cover removed for inspection). Code:

options.B: C2 — exposed live terminal could be inadvertently energised in maintenance
options.C: C1 — currently exposed, accessible live terminal

questions.explanation: Currently accessible live terminal = C1 (basic protection failed). Make safe by removing the MCB and blanking the way.

questions.prompt: Cable concealed in stud wall, route unknown, no detection possible. Code:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Unknown route compliance is FI. Use cable detection or open-up access to confirm safe-zone / depth requirements; the EICR is Unsatisfactory until the investigation is complete.

questions.prompt: Recently extended dishwasher socket without RCD additional protection. Code:

options.B: C2 — current edition requires RCD on accessible socket-outlets

questions.explanation: Modern installation work must comply with current edition. New socket-outlet without 30 mA RCD additional protection is C2; remedy by adding RCD or RCBO promptly.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a recently installed PV array where the AC isolator label says '230 V AC' but the wiring shows DC connections from PV array to inverter. Code:

options.B: C2 — incorrect labelling could result in unsafe isolation procedure

questions.explanation: Incorrect isolation labelling on a PV system is potentially dangerous in emergency or maintenance scenarios. C2 — relabel correctly with DC ratings and verify the isolator's compliance with PV requirements.

questions.prompt: Junction box screw missing, lid loose but in place, no live parts currently exposed. Code:

options.B: C2 — basic protection at risk of failure

questions.explanation: A loose lid that could fall away in normal use exposes a foreseeable progression to live-parts exposure. C2 — refit the screw, check the joint quality. C1 if the lid is already off and live parts are accessible.

questions.prompt: Earth electrode resistance measured 200 Ω on a TT system (typical limit ~200 Ω depending on protective device, but 30 mA RCD provides protection). Record:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory if the 30 mA RCD provides correct fault protection within disconnection times

questions.explanation: On TT systems with 30 mA RCD, the earth electrode resistance can be relatively high (BS 7671 historically allowed up to ~200 Ω with stable readings) provided the RCD operates correctly. Satisfactory if testing confirms RCD performance.

questions.prompt: Old mortice-tail bonding clamp on water service (legacy clamp on lead pipe). Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (replace with BS 951 clamp)

questions.explanation: Where continuity is intact and the bond is mechanically sound, an older clamp is typically C3 — replace with BS 951 type. If continuity is suspect or the clamp is compromised, the call lifts to C2.

questions.prompt: Exposed live conductor at a domestic ceiling rose (basic insulation breached, accessible if rose cover removed). Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — basic protection failed at an accessible position

questions.explanation: Exposed live parts under a removable cover are accessible during normal maintenance / lamp change. C1 — isolate, label, notify duty holder same day.

questions.prompt: Outdoor luminaire with damaged seal, water ingress visible, basic insulation intact. Code:

options.B: C2 — IP rating compromised, foreseeable progression to fault

questions.explanation: IP rating breach with intact insulation is C2 — foreseeable progression to insulation failure. Replace the seal or the fitting promptly. If the fault has already produced exposed live parts or earth leakage, C1.

questions.prompt: Domestic dwelling with TT system and 30 mA RCD that fails to trip at any test current. Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — TT depends on RCD for fault protection

questions.explanation: TT systems rely on RCDs for fault clearance because earth electrode loop impedance is too high for an MCB. An inoperative RCD on TT means no fault protection — C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Bonding clamp on metallic water service in good condition, continuity verified. Record:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Bonding present, in good condition, continuity verified = Satisfactory. The schedule entry records the bond's presence and condition.

questions.prompt: Domestic CU with mixed manufacturer MCBs / RCBOs, all functioning correctly. Code:

options.B: C3 — manufacturer mixing typically a conformance recommendation rather than immediate danger

questions.explanation: Mixing devices outside the CU's listed range is a manufacturer-conformance issue. Where protective measures still operate correctly, the typical call is C3 — recommendation to fit matched / listed devices.

questions.prompt: RCD bypassed (output terminals jumpered together to defeat tripping). Code:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Deliberate defeat of a protective device is C1 with on-site make-safe and same-day notification. Restore the RCD's functionality and re-test.

questions.prompt: BS 3036 fuse on a 30 A ring final, ADS times not met (Zs too high). Code:

options.B: C2 — disconnection time not met by protective device

questions.explanation: BS 3036 fuses can meet ADS where Zs is low enough; if Zs exceeds the limit, ADS is impaired — C2. Remedy by replacing with HBC fuse or MCB / RCBO and verifying Zs.

questions.prompt: Single C2 + ten C3s on an EICR — overall outcome:

options.B: Unsatisfactory because of the C2

questions.explanation: Any C2 = Unsatisfactory. C3 quantity does not affect the binary outcome; the duty holder's regulatory clock starts running on the C2.

questions.prompt: EICR observation 'Boiler-room circuits not inspected — locked, key with FM contractor unavailable'. Outcome impact:

options.B: Outcome reflects what was inspected; the limitation explicitly excludes those circuits from scope

questions.explanation: Agreed limitations carve out scope. The EICR's outcome reflects the inspected items only; the duty holder must arrange follow-up access for the missed circuits to fill the gap.

questions.prompt: Foil substituting for a rewireable fuse — duty holder's response is required:

options.B: Same-day make-safe, immediate replacement with correct fuse / device, written confirmation when complete

questions.explanation: C1 demands same-day make-safe (already done by the inspector if accessible). Permanent fix follows promptly with written confirmation. The 28-day clock applies under PRS Regs but the duty holder must act faster on a known C1.

questions.prompt: On an EICR, an item the inspector has previously coded C2 and that has now been remediated should be coded:

options.B: Recorded as remediated; the new EICR coding the current observed condition (typically Satisfactory if the remedy was effective)

questions.explanation: Each EICR captures current condition. A previously fixed C2 that is now compliant is Satisfactory on the new report. The previous observation lives in the previous report; the new one doesn't carry it forward.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an exposed conductor at the back of a luminaire's flex outlet, protruding through the protective sleeve. Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — exposed live conductor at an accessible location

questions.explanation: Exposed live conductor at an accessible point is C1. Isolate, label, notify duty holder same day.

questions.prompt: Domestic CU has a small surface scratch on the door, otherwise sound. Record:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — cosmetic only, no protective measure compromised

questions.explanation: Cosmetic scratches that don't affect IP rating, basic protection or fire containment are not coded. The inspector may note the scratch in the schedule for completeness; the result is Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Cable at <50 mm in plaster, in a safe zone, no RCD additional protection but the installation is from a long-standing installation predating the requirement. Code (typical):

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (current edition exceeds original requirement)

questions.explanation: Cable in a safe zone is partially covered by the safe-zone protection; the BS 7671 RCD-or-mechanical-protection requirement applies more strictly outside safe zones. Installation predating the requirement is typically C3 — improvement recommended (add 30 mA RCD).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with no labels at all. Code (typical):

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (correct identification per BS 7671 514.1.1)

questions.explanation: Missing identification is typically C3 — apply correct labels per BS 7671 514.1.1. Where misidentification could cause unsafe maintenance switching, the call lifts to C2.

questions.prompt: Schedule of Test Results shows R1+R2 of 0.43 Ω + Ze of 0.18 Ω = Zs 0.61 Ω; protective device's Zs limit (Type B 32 A) is 1.37 Ω. Record:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Zs 0.61 Ω vs limit 1.37 Ω = comfortable margin. Schedule entry records the values; no observation needed.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a damaged sheath at the entry to a metal back box; basic insulation intact; cable in dry, accessible location. Code:

options.B: C2 — mechanical protection compromised, foreseeable progression

questions.explanation: Damaged sheath at enclosure entry compromises mechanical protection; future vibration / movement could expose live parts. C2 — re-make the termination correctly. If basic insulation is already breached, C1.

questions.prompt: Privately rented dwelling EICR finds C2 missing main bonding to gas service. Landlord must remediate within:

options.B: 28 days from inspection (or sooner if specified)

questions.explanation: PRS Regs 2020: 28 days from inspection for any Unsatisfactory outcome (C1/C2/FI). Written confirmation supplied to tenant within 28 days of completion; local authority within 7 days of any written request.

questions.prompt: An EICR for a non-domestic premises identifies six C3s and no C1/C2/FI. Outcome:

options.B: Satisfactory — improvements recommended; duty holder plans them per HSWA / EAWR

questions.explanation: C3 quantity does not affect the binary outcome. Satisfactory result; duty holder plans improvements as part of normal maintenance / capital programme.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a damaged cable hung over a sharp metal edge in a cupboard, sheath chafed but basic insulation intact. Code:

options.B: C2 — mechanical protection compromised, foreseeable progression

questions.explanation: Chafed sheath with intact basic insulation is C2 — foreseeable progression to exposed live parts. Re-route the cable or apply mechanical protection. C1 if basic insulation is already breached.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit's protective device coordination issue — measured Zs is 1.4 Ω, BS 7671 Table 41.3 limit for Type B 16 A (5 s) is 1.37 Ω. Code:

options.B: C2 — Zs marginally above limit, ADS may not operate within required time

questions.explanation: Above limit Zs is potentially dangerous (C2). The inspector may use FI if there is genuine uncertainty about instrument tolerance / temperature correction. Remedy by reducing Zs (cable, terminations) or upgrading the protective device.

questions.prompt: Domestic CU is metal-clad, on a brick wall, with all terminations checked and clean. Record:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — typical compliant installation per current edition

questions.explanation: Metal CU on a non-combustible support with intact terminations is the configuration current BS 7671 expects for new installations. Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit with no CPC (older 1.0 mm² T cable, no earth). Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection essentially absent on the circuit
options.C: C1 (likely if circuit feeds Class I metalwork accessible to ordinary persons)
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed conditions

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement: a circuit with no CPC feeding Class II only (luminaires) may be C2; a circuit feeding Class I socket-outlets accessible to ordinary persons lifts to C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Outdoor socket-outlet at a dwelling, no RCD additional protection, no IP rating compromised, in active use. Code:

options.B: C2 — outdoor sockets used by ordinary persons require RCD additional protection

questions.explanation: Outdoor sockets are exposed to conditions where shock risk is higher and ordinary users may plug in portable equipment. Missing 30 mA RCD additional protection is therefore potentially dangerous and is normally coded C2.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a single ceiling rose with a connecting tail of solid copper visibly twisted to a flex tail with no terminal. Code:

options.B: C2 — joint not made in suitable terminal
options.C: C1 if the joint is exposed and accessible to a finger
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether the joint is currently accessible

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement: a tape-insulated, accessible joint is C2 if not currently exposed; if the joint is accessible to a finger, the call is C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic site, the inspector identifies a C2 and the duty holder commits to remediation within 14 days. The EICR overall outcome:

options.B: Remains Unsatisfactory at the time of inspection; the commitment is documented but the report records observed condition

questions.explanation: The EICR records the observed condition. Even with a remediation plan, the C2 makes the outcome Unsatisfactory until verified-remedy paperwork closes the loop.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a heavy load on a ring final (multiple high-current appliances) with the cable visibly warm but not discoloured. Code:

options.B: C2 if measured load exceeds cable rating; C3 if within rating

questions.explanation: Warm cable in itself is not a coding trigger; the test is whether load exceeds cable Iz under the actual installation method. If overload protection is not coordinated, C2; if within rating but warm, the inspector may note for the duty holder but Satisfactory unless a defect is identified.

questions.prompt: EICR observation 'Cable concealed in stud wall, route unknown' coded FI. Subsequent investigation finds the cable in safe zones with no mechanical protection issues. Resolution:

options.B: Issue written confirmation that the FI investigation found no defect; the EICR is updated / a follow-up record produced

questions.explanation: FI sometimes resolves with no actual defect found. Written confirmation closes the regulatory loop without further action. The duty holder retains the original EICR + investigation evidence as the compliance record.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic kitchen with two RCBOs (ring final and lights) and no main RCD. The protective scheme is otherwise sound. Record:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory if the RCBOs provide additional protection on the circuits used by ordinary persons

questions.explanation: RCBOs provide both fault protection and additional protection on individual circuits. A main RCD is not required where each accessible circuit has its own RCBO. Satisfactory if the protective scheme works correctly.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a privately rented dwelling with a 4-year-old satisfactory EICR. The next inspection is recommended in 1 year (was originally 5-year recommendation, then later inspector pulled in due to environment). Landlord obligation:

options.B: Commission new EICR within 1 year per the inspector's pulled-in recommendation

questions.explanation: PRS Regs 2020 follow the inspector's recommendation. If the inspector pulled the interval in, the landlord must comply with the shorter interval — extending to 5 years would breach the regulations.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit with an RCBO that fails to operate at 1×IΔn within 5 seconds. Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection performance impaired
options.C: C1 if the RCBO is the sole protective measure on accessible circuits used by ordinary persons
options.D: Either B or C depending on protective scheme

questions.explanation: RCBO failure mirrors RCD failure. C2 typical, lifting to C1 where the device is the sole guarantor of fault protection on circuits used by ordinary persons.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with a metal CU, all RCBOs, surge protection device (SPD) status indicator showing 'replace'. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (replace SPD module)

questions.explanation: An SPD past end-of-life still allows the rest of the installation to operate; the surge protection function is lost but the installation is otherwise compliant. Typical call is C3 — replace the SPD module promptly.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an active arc visible inside a metal CU, with the cover removed for inspection. Action:

options.B: Isolate the CU at the main switch / DNO upstream as appropriate, label, notify duty holder same day, code C1

questions.explanation: Active arcing is danger present. Isolate at the safest upstream point, label, notify duty holder, code C1 with a clear description. Same-day notification is non-negotiable.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with seven C2s and three C3s. The duty holder under HSWA / EAWR must:

options.B: Address the C2s with a risk-based remedial plan promptly; plan C3s as part of routine improvement; document the prioritisation

questions.explanation: C2s drive the Unsatisfactory result and demand prompt action under HSWA / EAWR risk-based principles. C3s are improvements to plan over time. Documentation of the prioritisation supports compliance with the regulations.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Earthing conductor present at MET; no main protective bonding to incoming water service (metallic, confirmed extraneous-conductive-part)'. Code:

options.B: C2 — main bonding requirement not met
options.D: Satisfactory because earthing conductor is present

questions.explanation: Bonding and earthing serve different functions. Main bonding to extraneous-conductive-parts is required to maintain equipotential during a fault. Absence is potentially dangerous (C2).

sections.title: Section 5 — Condition Reporting: Merged Observation Scenarios

questions.prompt: A detached metal-framed workshop is supplied from a dwelling TN-C-S/PME earthing system. It has extraneous-conductive-parts, a water pipe entering from underground, a small DB and 30 mA RCBOs. No local electrode is present. What is the key issue?

options.A: 30 mA RCBOs remove all PME open-PEN risks
options.B: Metal-framed buildings cannot ever be supplied electrically
options.C: The only issue is whether sockets have shutters
options.D: Open-PEN risk and exported PME touch voltage must be assessed, along with bonding, extraneous parts, CPC adequacy, ADS and simultaneous contact risks

questions.explanation: An open PEN on PME can raise connected metalwork above true Earth. RCDs do not necessarily operate for that condition. Classification depends on bonding, extraneous-conductive-parts, supply arrangement, outdoor contact risk and whether a TT arrangement or other mitigation is needed. Use FI if the risk cannot be verified.

questions.prompt: A domestic EV charge point is connected to a TN-C-S supply. No open-PEN detection device is visible, no earth electrode is present and no documentation is available. The charger is outdoors on a driveway. What is the best EICR outcome?

options.A: Automatically C1 because all EV chargers on PME are immediately dangerous
options.B: No code because all modern chargers secretly contain every protective device
options.C: FI until make/model, installation details and the Section 722 protective measure are verified; if no compliant open-PEN or equivalent measure exists, report accordingly, commonly C3 unless additional danger exists
options.D: N/A because EV chargers are appliances only

questions.explanation: Many EV chargers have built-in open-PEN protection that is not obvious externally, so FI is often correct until verified. If no compliant protective measure exists, report the non-compliance. More serious coding may be justified where there are additional defects, damaged equipment, ineffective earthing or manufacturer-prohibited conditions.

questions.prompt: A house has solar PV, battery storage and MCBs that appear unidirectional. The battery can export into the installation. Labels are incomplete and the circuit chart does not show the alternative source. Which answer is best?

options.A: Record incomplete alternative-source labelling and circuit chart as C3; use FI for unclear protective-device suitability, or C2 if a device is confirmed unsuitable for bidirectional current/fault conditions
options.B: Ignore it because PV and batteries are outside BS 7671
options.C: Automatically C1 because all batteries are immediately dangerous
options.D: No code because current direction never matters to protective devices

questions.explanation: Alternative supplies need clear identification and isolation information. Protective devices must be suitable for the direction and nature of current flow. Missing labels/charts are commonly C3, while uncertainty over device suitability is FI. Confirmed unsuitable protection that can impair safety may be C2.

questions.prompt: In a block of flats, several consumer-unit and distribution-board cable entries pass through a fire-resisting wall into a common escape route. Gaps around trunking and cables are unsealed. No thermal damage is present. What is the best classification?

options.A: No reportable observation because fire stopping is building work only
options.B: Likely C2, because electrical penetrations have compromised fire compartmentation in a common escape route
options.C: C3 only in all cases because there is no thermal damage
options.D: N/A because common parts are never inspected

questions.explanation: Electrical work that breaches or fails to maintain a fire barrier can create a serious fire and smoke spread risk, especially in common escape routes. Even though the issue overlaps with building fire safety, it is still a reportable electrical-installation observation.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds an exposed live conductor at a domestic kitchen ceiling rose that is accessible when the rose cover is removed. Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — basic protection failed at an accessible position

questions.explanation: Exposed live parts under a removable cover are accessible during normal lamp change. C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Bathroom Zone 1 socket-outlet — BS 7671 status:

options.B: Generally not permitted (except shaver supply units to BS EN 61558-2-5 in some locations)

questions.explanation: BS 7671 701: Zone 1 generally prohibits socket-outlets except specific shaver supply units to BS EN 61558-2-5. Outside zones, sockets must be at least 3 m from the boundary of Zone 1 (in dwellings).

questions.prompt: An inspector finds a 30 mA RCBO trip times — 1×IΔn 250 ms, 5×IΔn 35 ms. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: ≤300 ms at 1×IΔn for fault protection and ≤40 ms at 5×IΔn for additional protection. Both readings are within limits = Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic shower circuit on 2.5 mm² T+E with a 32 A MCB. Cable Iz 27 A under method 100. Code:

options.B: C2 — overload protection not coordinated

questions.explanation: Cable Iz < In(device) means overload protection is not coordinated; the cable could be overloaded under normal operation. C2 — redesign protection or reduce load to match cable Iz.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit's polarity reversed at the consumer unit (line and neutral swapped). Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — single-pole MCB now in neutral, isolation does not break line

questions.explanation: Reversed polarity at the CU defeats single-pole isolation entirely. The line stays connected when the device opens — danger present, C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: On a domestic dwelling EICR, the inspector finds a Class II luminaire fitted with single-pole switch in the line conductor. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — Class II equipment doesn't require an earth and SP line switching is normal UK practice

questions.explanation: Class II equipment relies on double insulation rather than a CPC. SP line switching is correct UK practice. Confirm basic insulation and double-insulation labelling are intact and record Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: A 6 A Type B MCB on a lighting circuit has a measured Zs of 4.4 Ω. Table 41.3 limit for 0.4 s disconnection: 7.28 Ω. For 5 s disconnection (fixed equipment): 14.57 Ω. Most appropriate record:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory if the lighting circuit qualifies for 5 s disconnection (e.g. fixed equipment, distribution circuit) and Zs is comfortably within the relevant limit

questions.explanation: Lighting circuits feeding fixed equipment in dwellings can qualify for 5 s disconnection times. Zs 4.4 Ω is well within the 5 s limit. The inspector confirms the disconnection time required and records Satisfactory if comfortably within.

questions.prompt: Three 4 Ω resistors connected in series:

options.B: 4 Ω

questions.explanation: Series: RT = R1 + R2 + R3 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 Ω. Parallel of the same three would give 4/3 ≈ 1.33 Ω.

questions.prompt: A circuit's measured R1+R2 is 0.50 Ω; Ze 0.30 Ω; protective device 32 A Type B (limit 1.37 Ω). Calculated Zs:
questions.explanation: Zs = Ze + R1+R2 = 0.30 + 0.50 = 0.80 Ω. Comfortably within the 32 A Type B limit of 1.37 Ω; ADS will operate within required time.

questions.prompt: A multi-function tester is being checked before use. The lock-off probe shrouds are missing. Most appropriate action:

options.B: Replace the leads / probes with GS38-compliant items before testing

questions.explanation: GS38 requires test leads with proper finger barriers, short exposed tips and current-limited leads where appropriate. Missing shrouds compromise the safety of live testing — replace with compliant probes before continuing.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a TN-C-S installation with a missing PME warning notice at the consumer unit. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (warning / labelling)

questions.explanation: Missing safety / warning notices are typically C3. Add a PME / TN-C-S warning at the position of the main earthing terminal so future maintenance / DNO operations are correctly informed.

questions.prompt: A 230 V supply has a peak voltage of approximately 325 V. Insulation rated 'Cat II 300 V' is suitable for normal mains use because:

options.B: Cat II rating refers to peak voltage and includes design margin for mains operation

questions.explanation: Cat II 300 V tester insulation is rated for normal mains use including peak voltages and transient overvoltages typical of low-voltage installations downstream of socket-outlets.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic premises EICR, the inspector finds a Class I metal accessory body where the CPC has come loose at the terminal. Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection earth path impaired
options.C: C1 if the CPC is effectively open and the accessory metalwork is reachable by ordinary persons
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether continuity is intact

questions.explanation: BPG4: a loose CPC with continuity intact is C2 — re-tighten and verify; an effectively open CPC on Class I metalwork accessible to ordinary persons is C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic kitchen with a fixed cooker connection unit, the unit's outgoing connection terminations not visible (concealed behind appliance). Most appropriate action:

options.B: Withdraw appliance to inspect or record an Operational Limitation if access is not possible

questions.explanation: Concealed terminations behind appliances are common. The inspector either arranges withdrawal of the appliance or records an Operational Limitation. Coding without inspection / agreement is not appropriate.

questions.prompt: A circuit's R1+R2 reads 0.20 Ω at the point of testing. Cable resistance per metre at 20 °C is 0.0145 Ω/m for line and 0.0145 Ω/m for CPC for 4 mm² T+E. Cable length is approximately:

options.B: Approximately 14 metres

questions.explanation: R1+R2 ≈ 2 × 0.0145 × L, so L ≈ 0.20 / (2 × 0.0145) ≈ 6.9 m. The inspector can sense-check measured R1+R2 against expected length to identify discrepancies.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a kitchen extractor fan with a damaged supply cable, basic insulation breached, accessible. Code:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Breached basic insulation with accessible live parts = C1 with on-site make-safe. Isolate the circuit, label, notify duty holder same day.

questions.prompt: On a TT supply, BS 7671 typical maximum earth electrode resistance for stable, reliable RCD-based fault protection is approximately:

options.A: 200 Ω (with stable readings, RCD providing fault protection)
options.B: 50 Ω always

questions.explanation: On TT systems with RCD protection, BS 7671 historically allowed up to 200 Ω with stable readings, supporting reliable RCD operation. Lower values give greater margin and faster operation.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Bathroom mirror cabinet light fitting (Class II) installed in Zone 2'. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — Zone 2 typically permits IPX4-rated luminaires (Class II is appropriate)

questions.explanation: Zone 2 in BS 7671 701 typically permits IPX4-rated equipment including Class II luminaires. The inspector confirms the IP rating and class are correct for the zone and records Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit's RCD test confirms the test button trips the device but the inspector hasn't measured trip times. Most appropriate action:

options.A: Tick Satisfactory based on test button operation
options.B: Measure trip times at 1×IΔn (and 5×IΔn for additional protection) and record values; the test button only proves the test mechanism

questions.explanation: The test button is a mechanical check; it doesn't verify trip-time performance against BS 7671 limits. The inspector measures actual trip times and records them on the schedule.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with all RCBOs and a Type 2 SPD. The SPD status indicator shows 'replace'. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (replace SPD module)

questions.explanation: An SPD past end-of-life still allows the rest of the installation to operate; the surge protection function is lost but the installation is otherwise compliant. Typical call is C3 — replace the SPD module promptly.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'BS 1361 fuse on a 30 A ring final, ADS times verified within limit, conductors / terminations sound'. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory or C3 (improvement recommended) depending on inspector judgement; modern installations would typically use MCBs / RCBOs

questions.explanation: BS 1361 fuses are not in themselves a defect if they meet ADS requirements. The inspector may record Satisfactory if everything works, or C3 with a recommendation to consider modern protection — the call depends on the wider context.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a metal cable tray (extraneous-conductive-part) used to support insulated cables and not connected to protective earth. Code:

options.B: C2 — extraneous / exposed-part not earthed; foreseeable progression to fault

questions.explanation: Metal containment that could become live under fault is treated as exposed-conductive-part / extraneous-part and must be earthed. Absence of earthing is C2 — install dedicated CPC or bond to MET.

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, an inspector finds a circuit's IR test reading 200 MΩ between line and earth. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — comfortably above BS 7671 minimum (1 MΩ for in-service)

questions.explanation: 200 MΩ is comfortably above the 1 MΩ in-service minimum. Schedule entry records the value; no observation needed.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic premises, EICR Unsatisfactory with one C2 (overloaded ring final). Duty holder schedule under EAWR / HSWA:

options.B: Risk-based — promptly with documented prioritisation; non-domestic is not on the PRS Regs 28-day clock

questions.explanation: Non-domestic premises follow EAWR / HSWA risk-based principles. Promptly is the standard, supported by documented prioritisation. The 28-day clock is specific to PRS rented domestic dwellings.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit's protective device working at the limit of its operating envelope (Zs at limit, RCD trip times at limit). Most appropriate professional action:

options.B: Note the borderline operation, consider FI or recommend planned remedial work to give margin, document the position clearly

questions.explanation: At-limit operation is technically Satisfactory but lacks margin against future deterioration. The inspector may use FI if the reading is genuinely uncertain, or note the borderline position with a recommendation for proactive maintenance — exposing the duty holder's residual risk for informed decision.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds a hospital theatre circuit's CPC has corroded to a fragile state at the busbar; continuity is intermittent. Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection earth path unreliable
options.C: C1 — accessible exposed-conductive-parts of theatre equipment depend on this CPC
options.D: Either B or C depending on continuity testing and accessibility

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement: an intermittent CPC providing some fault protection is C2; an effectively open CPC on Class I theatre equipment used by ordinary persons is C1. Hospital duty holders typically take an aggressive risk-based view.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 Section 701 zones: Zone 0 in a bath:

options.B: Above the bath

questions.explanation: Zone 0 = the inside of a bath / shower basin. Zone 1 extends to 2.25 m above the floor or top of the bath / shower; Zone 2 is the 0.6 m horizontal extension from Zone 1.

questions.prompt: An EICR's Schedule of Test Results shows a circuit with 'IR open circuit' between line and earth. Most appropriate interpretation:

options.B: IR is so high the meter cannot resolve a value (effectively perfect insulation) — record as >999 MΩ or Satisfactory

questions.explanation: 'Open circuit' on an IR test means very high resistance — effectively perfect insulation. Record as >999 MΩ (or whatever the instrument shows) and Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a 5 m extension lead trailing through a corridor used by ordinary persons, with multiple appliances daisy-chained. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3 on the EICR
options.C: Outside fixed-installation EICR scope; the inspector may flag it in the summary as a hazard but it doesn't drive a coded observation

questions.explanation: Portable / non-fixed equipment is outside the fixed-installation EICR scope. The inspector may note the hazard in the summary or recommend a separate review (PAT-style) but it doesn't drive a coded observation on the fixed installation.

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, an inspector finds a 13 A plug fuse blown on a connected appliance. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Outside fixed-installation EICR scope; appliances are PAT territory

questions.explanation: Plug fuses on portable appliances are PAT scope, not fixed-installation EICR scope. The inspector may note the issue informally but it doesn't drive a coded EICR observation.

questions.prompt: An EICR identifies a circuit's R1+R2 reading much higher than expected for the cable length. Most appropriate next step:

options.B: Investigate for high-resistance terminations; if cause cannot be determined during inspection, code FI

questions.explanation: Anomalously high R1+R2 typically indicates a high-resistance termination somewhere on the circuit. The inspector investigates by re-tightening / re-testing; if the cause cannot be determined during the visit, FI is appropriate.

questions.prompt: On a 230 V supply, the prospective short-circuit current at the origin is measured at 1.2 kA. The protective device's breaking capacity must be:

options.B: At least 6 kA (BS EN 60898 standard rating typically used in UK domestic installations)

questions.explanation: BS EN 60898 standard MCBs are rated to 6 kA — comfortably above typical domestic prospective short-circuit currents. Industrial settings may need higher Icu / Ics ratings.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a circuit feeding outdoor 230 V garden lighting, RCD additional protection in place, IP rating of luminaires correct. Outcome:

options.B: Satisfactory if no other defects observed; the design appears compliant

questions.explanation: RCD additional protection on garden lighting + correct IP rating of luminaires + no other defects = Satisfactory. The schedules support the result.

questions.prompt: Five 10 Ω resistors connected in parallel:

options.B: 2 Ω

questions.explanation: RT = R / n = 10 / 5 = 2 Ω. The same five in series would total 50 Ω.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a damaged metal-clad CU door, IP rating compromised. Code:

options.B: C2 — IP rating compromised, foreseeable progression to fault

questions.explanation: IP rating breach with intact internals is C2 — replace the door / repair the seal. C1 if the breach has already exposed live parts or led to internal damage.

questions.prompt: On an EICR, an item the inspector cannot definitively assess (e.g. a sealed appliance enclosure that cannot be opened on the day) is most appropriately:

options.B: Recorded as FI — further investigation required to determine condition

questions.explanation: FI captures evidence of a possible defect that the inspector cannot diagnose during the inspection. The investigation closes the loop; the EICR is Unsatisfactory until it is done.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds a damaged armoured cable gland on a school's playground supply (cable to outdoor security lighting), inner cores intact. Code (typical):

options.B: C2 (likely) — mechanical / earthing reliability of SWA reduced
options.C: C1 if cores damaged exposing live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: BPG4 again invites judgement: damaged gland with intact cores = C2; damaged gland with breached basic insulation = C1 with on-site make-safe. School / public-access setting may push the inspector toward stricter coding.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a 30 mA RCD that does not respond to the test button or to the multi-function tester. Code:

options.B: C2
options.C: C1 — protective device non-functional, sole protective measure on accessible circuits
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether the RCD is the sole protective measure

questions.explanation: BPG4: non-functional RCD where it is one of multiple protective layers may be C2; where it is the sole guarantor against direct contact (e.g. cables in safe zones with no earthed mechanical protection), the call lifts to C1.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic EICR, an inspector finds an underground cable's gland-end visibly damp, with corrosion at the gland and basic insulation visibly degraded. Code:

options.B: C2 — environmental damage progressing toward fault
options.C: C1 if basic insulation breach is exposing live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: BPG4: contained corrosion with no exposed live parts = C2 with prompt remedy; exposed live parts = C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU's spare way with the MCB removed and the way blanked correctly. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — correctly blanked spare way is compliant

questions.explanation: Correctly blanked spare way maintains basic protection / IP rating of the CU. Satisfactory; the schedule entry confirms the spare way's status.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a 32 A radial circuit on 6 mm² T+E, run in conduit clipped direct (method 100 in BS 7671 Appendix 4). Cable Iz approximately 47 A. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — cable Iz comfortably exceeds device In

questions.explanation: Cable Iz 47 A > device In 32 A, with margin for derating factors. Schedule entry records the conductor / installation method and Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Plastic CU on combustible (wooden) backboard' in a domestic dwelling, no other defects, current BPG4 typical code:

options.B: C2 (older BPG4 default)
options.C: C3 (current BPG4 default for non-DSEAR domestic)

questions.explanation: Current BPG4 places intact plastic CUs on wooden backboards (non-DSEAR domestic) at C3. Earlier guidance was C2; the consensus moved as fire-spread concerns shifted to termination quality and metal-CU containment for new work.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an undersized main bonding conductor (4 mm² where 10 mm² required for current PME supply). Code:

options.B: C2 — main bonding conductor inadequate for fault currents

questions.explanation: Undersized main bonding cannot reliably maintain equipotential during a fault. C2 — replace with adequately sized conductor per BS 7671 Table 54.8 (typically 10 mm² for main bonding on a TN-C-S supply with 16 mm² earthing conductor).

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, an inspector finds a metal-clad CU with all RCBOs, surge protection device fitted and working. Outcome (no other observations):

options.B: Satisfactory — modern compliant configuration

questions.explanation: Modern compliant configuration with no observations = Satisfactory. The recommended next-inspection date is set per BPG4 / GN3 (typically 5 years for a domestic dwelling).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a cable that was previously coded C2 but has now been remediated and re-tested. The new EICR records:

options.B: Satisfactory if the remedy is effective; the previous C2 lives in the previous report
options.C: C3 to acknowledge the previous concern

questions.explanation: Each EICR captures current condition. A previously fixed C2 that is now compliant is Satisfactory on the new report. The previous observation lives in the previous report; the new report doesn't carry it forward.

questions.prompt: An office EICR finds a 230 V mains-fed network switch in a desk-mounted server cabinet, fed via a portable extension lead. Schedule entry:

options.A: C2 because of the extension lead
options.B: C3 on the fixed installation if the supply socket is satisfactory; the extension lead is outside fixed-installation scope but may be flagged in the summary

questions.explanation: The fixed installation's role ends at the socket-outlet. The extension lead is portable equipment outside the EICR's coding scope; the inspector may flag the daisy-chain hazard in the summary but it doesn't drive a coded observation.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic premises, the inspector finds a high-fault-level supply with a CU containing 6 kA standard MCBs. Code:

options.B: C2 — protective device breaking capacity inadequate for the supply

questions.explanation: If the supply's prospective fault current exceeds the protective device's breaking capacity, the device cannot reliably clear a fault. C2 — replace with appropriately rated devices (e.g. 10 kA, 25 kA or backup-fused arrangement).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic kitchen with a previously-installed RCBO on the ring final, and a separate non-RCD-protected MCB on the lighting circuit. Modern dwelling. Schedule entry:

options.B: C2 if cables are also outside safe zones / unprotected; C3 if otherwise compliant

questions.explanation: Lighting circuit without RCD in a modern dwelling is typically C3 — improvement recommended (current edition expects RCD on lighting in dwellings). If cables are also outside safe zones or otherwise unprotected, the call rises to C2.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Bonding clamp on water service is BS 951 compliant, mechanically sound, continuity verified'. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: BS 951 clamp, mechanically sound, continuity verified = Satisfactory. The schedule records the clamp type and condition.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling EICR with one C2 (missing main bonding to gas service). The remedy is:

options.B: Install main protective bonding conductor (typically 10 mm²) from MET to gas service entry, using BS 951 clamp; verify continuity; issue written confirmation

questions.explanation: The remedy for missing main bonding is to install the bonding conductor and clamp, verify continuity, and confirm in writing. The PRS Regs 2020 28-day clock applies; the duty holder commissions the work and supplies confirmation to the tenant within 28 days of completion.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds a circuit feeding a domestic shower with no RCD protection. The shower is 9.5 kW with cable run partly through stud walls. Code:

options.B: C2 — required additional protection / cable-route protection not provided

questions.explanation: Modern shower circuits require 30 mA RCD additional protection (or RCBO). Cable run through stud walls without mechanical protection or RCD adds C2 weight. Remedy by adding 30 mA RCD or RCBO.

questions.prompt: On a 230 V single-phase circuit, voltage drop on a 10 m run of 4 mm² T+E carrying 25 A (typical mV/A/m ≈ 11 mV/A/m). Calculated voltage drop:

options.B: Approximately 2.75 V

questions.explanation: Voltage drop = mV/A/m × A × m / 1000 = 11 × 25 × 10 / 1000 = 2.75 V. Within BS 7671 typical limits (3% for lighting / 5% for power on 230 V).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a hospital ward circuit with a Schedule of Test Results showing all readings within BS 7671 limits and no visible defects. Outcome:

options.B: Satisfactory if no observations are recorded

questions.explanation: All readings within limits + no observations = Satisfactory. The Schedule of Test Results supports the outcome; the inspector signs and dates the report.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 Section 701 zone for a basin-type shower with rim 1500 mm above the floor: Zone 1 extends to:

options.B: 2250 mm above the floor (the 'standard' Zone 1 ceiling)

questions.explanation: Zone 1 typically extends to 2.25 m above the floor or top of the bath / shower (whichever is higher). Above 2.25 m the space is Zone 2 (where it qualifies).

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an EICR Schedule of Inspections marked ✓ on items the inspector did not actually check. The risk is:

options.B: The inspector takes responsibility for an item they have not verified, and the report is misleading

questions.explanation: ✓ creates a positive declaration of acceptable condition. Marking it without inspection is fraudulent and exposes the inspector to civil and regulatory liability. Use N/A or record an agreed limitation instead.

questions.prompt: On a TN-S supply, Ze measured at 0.20 Ω. R1+R2 measured 0.85 Ω. Calculated Zs:
questions.explanation: Zs = Ze + R1+R2 = 0.20 + 0.85 = 1.05 Ω. Compare with Table 41.3 limit for the protective device to verify ADS adequacy.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a school's electrical isolator that does not actually de-energise the labelled circuit when operated (mis-installed). Code:

options.B: C2 — isolation switching incomplete; safety device misleading
options.C: C1 if maintenance reliance on the isolator could leave operatives at exposed live parts
options.D: Either B or C depending on the circumstances

questions.explanation: BPG4: a misleading isolator is C2 with prompt remedy; if there is foreseeable risk that maintenance staff would rely on it for live work, the call lifts to C1. School premises with multiple maintenance contractors invite stricter coding.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with one RCBO that fails the 5×IΔn test (no trip within 40 ms) but passes the 1×IΔn test (300 ms). Code:

options.B: C2 — additional protection performance impaired

questions.explanation: Failure at 5×IΔn means additional protection performance (≤40 ms) is not met. The fault-protection function (1×IΔn) operates correctly but additional protection for direct contact is unreliable. C2 — replace the device.

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, the inspector finds a circuit's RCBO that has had its test button pressed but the RCBO did not trip. Subsequent live-test instrument confirms inoperative. Code:

options.B: C2 — protective device non-functional, but other layers of protection may still apply
options.C: C1 — sole protective measure on accessible circuits used by ordinary persons
options.D: Either B or C depending on whether RCBO is the sole protective measure

questions.explanation: BPG4 invites judgement: failure where RCBO is one of multiple protective layers may be C2; where it is the sole guarantor against direct contact (e.g. on accessible socket-outlets) the call lifts to C1.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'EICR document set incomplete: Schedule of Inspections present but Schedule of Test Results not held by duty holder' on a previous report. Code on current EICR:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (documentation gap on prior report)

questions.explanation: Missing previous documentation is a C3 documentation finding. The current inspector produces a complete EICR + schedules; the past gap is recorded but not coded as a present danger.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with active condensation visible inside a metal CU, surface corrosion at the busbar; no exposed live parts. Code:

options.B: C2 — environmental conditions degrading equipment, foreseeable progression

questions.explanation: Active moisture / corrosion in a CU is C2 — relocate / replace the CU, address the environmental cause. Active arcing or exposed live parts would lift to C1.

questions.prompt: Two 6 Ω resistors in series, then in parallel with a 3 Ω resistor:
An EICR observation 'Domestic dwelling with mortice-tail bonding clamp on lead water service pipe, mechanically sound, continuity verified'. Code:

options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (replace with BS 951 clamp)

questions.explanation: Older clamps are typically C3 — replace with BS 951 type for current compliance. Where continuity is intact and the clamp is sound, it functions but is not best-practice.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with all RCBOs and a Type 2 SPD. Schedule of Test Results clean, no other observations. Outcome:

options.B: Satisfactory — modern compliant configuration

questions.explanation: Modern compliant configuration + clean schedules + no observations = Satisfactory. The recommended next-inspection date is set per BPG4 / GN3.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic premises EICR, the inspector finds a 3-phase 32 A motor circuit with the motor's earth lug visibly loose, continuity intermittent. Code:

options.B: C2 — fault protection earth path unreliable
options.C: C1 if continuity is effectively lost and motor body becomes potentially live
options.D: Either B or C depending on continuity testing

questions.explanation: BPG4: loose-but-intermittent CPC = C2 with prompt remedy; effectively open CPC on Class I motor body accessible to maintenance staff = C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic kitchen with a fixed cooker hood (Class I) with the CPC connected and continuity verified. The cooker hood is fed from a switched fused spur. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — Class I appliance correctly fed and earthed

questions.explanation: Class I appliance with verified CPC, fed from a fused spur (rated for the load) = correctly installed. Schedule entry confirms the configuration; Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a 230 V circuit where measured Ze is 0.10 Ω, R1+R2 0.50 Ω, Zs 0.60 Ω; protective device is Type B 32 A (Table 41.3 limit 1.37 Ω). Schedule entry:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Zs 0.60 Ω vs limit 1.37 Ω = comfortable margin. Schedule entry records the values; ADS will operate within required time.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Recently installed PV array, no AC isolator label visible'. Code:

options.B: C2 — labelling required for emergency isolation

questions.explanation: PV systems require correct AC and DC isolation labelling. Missing label is potentially dangerous (C2) — emergency responders need to identify and isolate correctly.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a 13 A current passing through a conductor of resistance 0.3 Ω. Power dissipated:
questions.explanation: P = I²R = 13² × 0.3 = 169 × 0.3 = 50.7 W. The I²R loss drives cable heating — and is what makes a loose termination a developing fire risk.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a school with a recently extended IT room and a new circuit installed without certification. The lack of EIC for the new circuit is recorded as:

options.B: C2

questions.explanation: Lack of original certification is a documentation issue. C3 — improvement recommended (obtain certification or document the works retrospectively). The inspector still tests the circuit and codes any technical defects separately.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Cable run in trunking with 70% fill factor exceeding BS 7671 reference values'. Code (typical):

options.B: C2 — derating not addressed, cable could be overloaded
options.C: C3 — improvement recommended (verify cable rating with derating factors)

questions.explanation: High fill factor reduces cable Iz via derating. C3 typical (verify cable rating with derating, redesign if necessary). C2 if measured load already exceeds derated cable rating.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with a 30 mA RCD that protects the entire installation (one main RCD). Half the circuits are non-essential. Code:

options.A: C2 — single RCD protects too many circuits
options.B: C3 — improvement recommended (modern installation would use separate RCBOs / split RCDs to reduce nuisance-tripping impact)
options.D: Satisfactory if the protection works correctly

questions.explanation: A single main RCD protecting all circuits was acceptable practice; modern installations use split-load or RCBOs to limit the impact of nuisance trips. If the RCD works correctly, Satisfactory; the inspector may note a recommendation for split protection.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Damaged sheath at entry to switch box; basic insulation intact; cable not flexing'. Code:

options.B: C2 — mechanical protection compromised, foreseeable progression

questions.explanation: Damaged sheath at enclosure entry compromises mechanical protection. C2 — re-make the termination. C1 if basic insulation is also breached.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with all observations addressed since the previous EICR (which was Unsatisfactory). The current EICR records:

options.B: Outcome based on currently observed condition; if remediation is verified and no new defects are found, Satisfactory

questions.explanation: Each EICR captures current condition. Verified remediation of previous Unsatisfactory items + no new defects = Satisfactory current outcome. The previous report's Unsatisfactory result lives in that report; the new one is independent.

questions.prompt: On a non-domestic site, the duty holder shows the inspector remediation evidence (invoices, photographs) for previous C2 items but no written confirmation from a qualified person. The inspector should:

options.A: Accept the evidence and issue Satisfactory
options.B: Recommend the duty holder obtain proper written confirmation; carry out their own inspection / testing of the remediated items as part of the new EICR

questions.explanation: Written confirmation from a qualified person is the standard compliance evidence. The new EICR may include re-inspection / re-test of the remediated items, with the inspector's own findings driving the outcome. The duty holder should keep the qualified-person confirmation as their compliance trail.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds an agricultural building's outdoor distribution board with seal failure and active water ingress, basic insulation visibly degrading. Code:

options.B: C2 — IP rating compromised, foreseeable progression to fault
options.C: C1 if basic insulation is breached and live parts exposed
options.D: Either B or C depending on observed condition

questions.explanation: Agricultural premises have stricter environmental requirements (BS 7671 705). Compromised IP rating with intact insulation is C2; breached insulation exposing live parts is C1 with on-site make-safe.

questions.prompt: BS 7671 Section 705 (agricultural / horticultural premises) typically requires:

options.A: Additional protection by 30 mA RCD for socket-outlet circuits up to 32 A
options.B: No RCD protection

questions.explanation: BS 7671 705 requires additional protection by 30 mA RCD for typical socket-outlet circuits in agricultural / horticultural premises, due to the wet, dirty, mechanically harsh environment that increases shock and fault risk.

questions.prompt: An inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a sub-main fed from a 100 A switch-fuse with HRC 80 A fuse links. Cable Iz is 75 A. Code:

options.B: C2 — overload protection not coordinated (In > Iz)

questions.explanation: Cable Iz < In(device) means overload protection is not coordinated; cable could be overloaded under normal operation. C2 — fit a smaller fuse link, upgrade cable, or reduce design current to match cable Iz.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a kitchen with a fixed cooker (45 A circuit), where the cooker control unit and a 13 A switched socket are combined. Cable to the cooker is 6 mm² T+E. Schedule entry:

options.A: C2 because of the combined cooker / socket unit
options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory if the protective device, cable size and load are correctly coordinated; combined cooker / socket units are acceptable

questions.explanation: Combined cooker control units with integrated 13 A socket are common UK practice. Schedule entry confirms cable size, protective device, polarity etc. Satisfactory if everything is correctly coordinated.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with a 100 A main switch fed from the DNO supply, with neutral conductor visibly broken at the cut-out (sealed by the DNO). The inspector should:

options.B: Notify the DNO immediately; the DNO's cut-out and meter tails up to the consumer's installation are the DNO's responsibility
options.C: Code C1 and ignore the boundary

questions.explanation: DNO equipment is the DNO's responsibility. The inspector notifies the DNO immediately for action on the cut-out; the inspector's coding applies to the consumer's installation downstream of the meter. Document the issue clearly on the EICR.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Domestic dwelling lighting circuit, no RCD additional protection, dwelling pre-dates current edition'. Code (typical, BPG4):

options.B: C2
options.C: C3 — improvement recommended (current edition exceeds original)

questions.explanation: BS 7671 not retrospective. Lighting circuit complying with original edition but not current is C3 — improvement recommended (add 30 mA RCD protection). C2 may apply if cables are also outside safe zones / unprotected.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with three RCBOs and three MCBs. The MCB-protected circuits feed kitchen socket-outlets. Code:

options.B: C2 — accessible socket-outlets without RCD additional protection

questions.explanation: Kitchen socket-outlets used by ordinary persons require RCD additional protection per current edition. MCB-only protection is C2 — replace MCBs with RCBOs or add RCD protection.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with a TT system, 30 mA RCD providing fault protection, earth electrode resistance 50 Ω. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — TT with RCD protection at acceptable electrode resistance

questions.explanation: TT system with 30 mA RCD providing fault protection at electrode resistance well within typical TT operating range = Satisfactory. The schedule records electrode resistance and RCD trip times.

questions.prompt: On a hospital EICR, an Operational Limitation has been recorded for theatre circuits that cannot be isolated. The duty holder's responsibility:

options.B: Plan a follow-up inspection in a maintenance window; until then, retain risk-based interim controls and document the position

questions.explanation: Operational limitations carve out scope; the duty holder retains the legal duty under HSWA / EAWR to ensure safety. They plan a maintenance window for the missed circuits and document interim risk controls.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Bathroom Zone 1 luminaire with IP44 rating' on a domestic dwelling. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — IP44 is acceptable for Zone 1 in BS 7671 701

questions.explanation: BS 7671 701: Zone 1 typically requires IPX4 / IP4X-rated equipment; IP44 satisfies this requirement. The schedule confirms the IP rating; Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a main switch fitted as a single-pole device on a 230 V single-phase supply. Code:

options.B: C2 — main switch should be DP (or all poles) for full isolation

questions.explanation: Main switches on 230 V single-phase supplies should be DP (line + neutral) to provide full isolation per BS 7671 537. SP main switches leave the neutral connected — potentially dangerous (C2) — replace with DP.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling with a 30 mA RCD providing additional protection, trip times 1×IΔn 290 ms, 5×IΔn 38 ms. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — within BS 7671 limits (≤300 ms / ≤40 ms)

questions.explanation: Both readings within limits = Satisfactory. The borderline trip time at 1×IΔn might invite a future check, but as recorded it satisfies BS 7671 disconnection time requirements.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Damaged extension lead in domestic kitchen, basic insulation visibly compromised'. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3 on the EICR
options.C: Outside fixed-installation EICR scope; portable equipment is PAT territory; the inspector may flag the hazard in the summary

questions.explanation: Extension leads are portable equipment outside the EICR's coding scope. The inspector may flag the hazard in the summary or recommend a separate review (PAT-style); fixed-installation EICR coding doesn't apply.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with all RCBOs and a Type 2 SPD with status indicator green (within service life). Schedule entry:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Modern compliant configuration with SPD within service life = Satisfactory. The schedule confirms SPD presence and status; the inspector includes a note about expected SPD service life for the duty holder's planning.

questions.prompt: On a 100 A PME supply with fault level 16 kA at the origin, the protective devices' breaking capacity must be:

options.B: ≥16 kA (matched to prospective fault current)

questions.explanation: Breaking capacity must equal or exceed prospective fault current. 6 kA standard MCBs would be inadequate; 10 kA / 16 kA / 25 kA devices or backup-fused arrangements would be required to safely interrupt a fault.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with a 3-phase 32 A motor circuit, all protective measures intact, R1+R2 verified, motor body earthed. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3

questions.explanation: Protective measures intact, schedules clean = Satisfactory. The motor circuit's specific test set (Zs, R1+R2, IR, RCD if fitted) supports the entry.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Bonding clamp on confirmed extraneous-conductive-part metallic gas pipe is loose, oxidised, but continuity intact'. Code:

options.B: C2 — mechanical / electrical reliability of bond reduced
options.C: C1 if continuity is intermittent or effectively lost
options.D: Either B or C depending on continuity testing

questions.explanation: BPG4: loose-but-continuous = C2 with prompt remedy; effectively open / lost = C1 with on-site make-safe. The inspector documents the actual continuity reading.

questions.prompt: On a domestic EICR, the inspector finds a circuit's MCB rating mismatched with a label that says different rating (label says 16 A, MCB is 32 A). Code:

options.B: C2 — incorrect identification could mislead future maintenance

questions.explanation: Mismatched label / device creates a foreseeable hazard during future maintenance — the wrong device could be installed if the label is trusted, leading to under-protected cable. C2 — correct the label or replace the device to match.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a non-domestic premises with an EICR that records two C2 observations and three C3 observations. The duty holder under HSWA / EAWR must:

options.A: Action all five within 28 days as for PRS dwellings
options.B: Address the C2s with a documented risk-based remedial plan promptly; plan C3s as part of routine improvement
options.C: Action only the most expensive one

questions.explanation: Non-domestic premises follow HSWA / EAWR risk-based principles. C2s drive prompt action with documented prioritisation; C3s are improvements to plan over time. The 28-day clock is specific to PRS Regs 2020 rented domestic dwellings.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Class II light fitting in the dwelling kitchen, single-pole switch on the line conductor, basic insulation and double-insulation labelling intact'. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — Class II equipment doesn't require an earth and SP line switching is normal UK practice

questions.explanation: Class II equipment relies on double insulation rather than CPC. SP line switching is correct UK practice. Confirm basic insulation and double-insulation labelling and record Satisfactory.

questions.prompt: On a 230 V supply, the prospective short-circuit current at the origin is 6 kA. A 6 kA breaking capacity MCB is fitted. Schedule entry:

options.B: C3
options.C: Satisfactory — breaking capacity equal to prospective fault current

questions.explanation: Breaking capacity = prospective fault current at the origin = 6 kA. The device can safely interrupt the maximum credible fault. Satisfactory; the schedule records both values.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic dwelling EICR with a previous Unsatisfactory result that the landlord acted on within 28 days. The current EICR is being prepared at the next 5-year interval. Outcome basis:

options.B: Independent assessment based on current observed condition
options.C: Pending until previous report is reviewed

questions.explanation: Each EICR is an independent snapshot. The current report reflects the current observed condition; the previous report's Unsatisfactory result and remediation are part of the historical record but don't predetermine the current outcome.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds a domestic CU with no main bonding to a confirmed extraneous-conductive-part metal water service. Code:

options.B: C2 — main bonding requirement not met

questions.explanation: Confirmed extraneous-conductive-part requires main bonding to maintain equipotential during a fault. Absence is potentially dangerous (C2) — install bonding sized per Table 54.8.

questions.prompt: Inspector finds an EICR with no observations and a recommended next-inspection date 5 years out. Outcome:

options.B: Satisfactory

questions.explanation: No observations + correctly set recommended interval + signed and dated = Satisfactory. The inspector's signature is a professional declaration that the schedules support the outcome.

questions.prompt: An EICR observation 'Inspector confirms all circuits inspected and tested per the agreed scope; one C2 (missing main bonding) and three C3 (improvement recommendations)'. Outcome and duty holder action under PRS Regs 2020:

options.B: Unsatisfactory because of the C2; remediate the C2 within 28 days from inspection, supply written confirmation to tenant within 28 days of completion; plan C3s over time

questions.explanation: Any C2 = Unsatisfactory. PRS Regs 2020: 28-day remediation clock from inspection; 28-day written-confirmation clock from completion. C3s are improvements to plan; no specific PRS clock applies to C3s alone.

scoring.label: Strong - exam-ready on GN3, EICR coding and defensible reporting
Pass - review missed interval, sampling, limitation or coding decisions
Needs targeted revision - re-read GN3 Chapter 3, BS 7671 Part 6 and BPG4
Major gaps - rebuild periodic inspection and condition reporting fundamentals first

priorities: C1, C2, C3 and FI must be applied from observed risk, not from how easy the remedial job looks.
Any C1, C2 or FI makes the EICR Unsatisfactory; C3 alone remains Satisfactory with improvement recommended.
Extent, sampling and limitations must be agreed, specific, recorded and revised when findings justify expansion.
Periodic inspection is judgement-led: select safe tests, justify live testing, and interpret readings against the existing installation condition.
Duty-holder and PRS duties matter: immediate danger notification, 28-day remedial rules, written confirmation and next-inspection recommendations.
